News.title: Hero 9/11 firefighter's family finally learn which tower he died in as new details emerge 25 years later
News.content:
Hero 9/11 firefighter's family finally learn which tower he died in as new details emerge 25 years later

EXCLUSIVE: Never before seen photos of hero 9/11 fireman Gary Geidel were found in disposable camera which was left in an attic bringing back emotional memories for his family

Gary Geidel

The family of a hero 9/11 firefighter are still uncovering new details of his death - 25 years after the tragic day.

‌



Gary Geidel’s body was never found. But his wife Tillie and their daughter, also called Tillie, have found out new information about where he was last seen. It appears Gary died in the South Tower not in the North Tower as previously thought.

‌



Incredibly, they even found a disposable camera with undeveloped film in their loft. When they had it developed, it had six photos of Gary which were taken in 2000 - a year before 9/11. They had never been seen them before and they brought back emotional memories ahead of the 25th anniversary.

‌



View 4 Images A never before seen photo of 9/11 fireman hero Gary Geidel

Tillie, jnr, has compiled an emotional book called: “9/11 Through The Eyes of A Daughter - The story of Gary Geidel an American hero.” She said: “I found an old camera in my attic and brought it to Walmart to be developed. I had no idea what was on the camera or if the photos were still okay to be developed.

"I was praying somehow my dad would be on the roll. I picked the pictures up, and started to flip through them, and there was a picture of my dad. He was in about six pictures on that roll. It was amazing how I found new pictures of him after 19 years. What a gift from God!”

‌



View 4 Images Tille Geidel and daughter Tillie Geidel - husband and dad Gary was a 9/11 firefighter hero (Image: Ian Vogler / Daily Mirror)

She added: “After years of searching through every video and photo of 9/11 I could get my hands on, we finally found my dad. A few people, including my aunt, sent my mom and I video footage of firemen on 9/11. The man they thought was my father turned out to be someone else, but we actually spotted my dad in the background.

“Turns out we were right all along, and he was never with Rescue One that morning. He was in the South Tower of the World Trade Center, not the North Tower. With my father's death being so public, this is one thing we get to have to ourselves. That was the footage leading up to my dad's last moments on this earth, and that is very private. I am still uncovering things since then.”

‌



View 4 Images 9/11 fireman hero Gary Geidel (Image: Tillie Geidel)

Shortly after 9/11 I went to interview Tillie at her and Gary’s home on Staten Island. Tillie jnr was just seven years old. Recalling the memory, she said: “I vividly remember you coming and I was up the stairs. Your photographer affectionately called me 'sausage' and I’ve always remembered that.

“It’s been very difficult for me and my mum. But we both remember my dad with great pride. We are so proud of him. We do feel he sends us messages - 'pennies from heaven' we call them."

‌



Her mum said: “I really only cope through my faith and my family. That's what keeps us going. Knowing that, you know, some day we know we're going to see him again. So it's not an easy road not having him there. It's an everyday struggle. It's an everyday thing.”

She added: “It’s particularly difficult in the run-up the anniversary. Things get really emotional, especially, you know, when the anniversary is coming up. It just, it builds, you know. You could feel it coming up. It's usually around mid-July.

View 4 Images

‌



"You could feel it, like, starting to build. Even though it's something that you live with every day, you know, I mean, you're not sitting there crying every day. It just becomes more and more intense. You know, you do live with it, but when it comes closer to the anniversary every year, it gets more intense.

“We are so, so extremely proud of him. He was such a good man. But not for just being a hero. For being a father, for being a family man. Yes, a family man first. And he was an all-around good person.

Article continues below

"If you ask anybody from where he came from or will work with. But anyone from the town of Tottenville. In the town, on his softball team, everywhere. No one ever had anything bad to say about him. His colleagues who survived have been very kind and supportive of us.”

News.title: Heathrow and Gatwick - live: More than 300 flights cancelled today after air traffic control glitch
News.content:
EasyJet, BA, Ryanair, KLM and Eurowings flights have all been cancelled at major airports including Heathrow and Gatwick today following the air traffic control issues on Tuesday

Flights are still being cancelled and delayed across the UK - after an air traffic control "technical issue" on Tuesday - as a Government minister said she did not believe the chaos was "unavoidable".

When asked whether Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander and Prime Minister still have confidence in NATS (National Air Traffic Services) CEO Martin Rolfe, a spokesperson said: "We have confidence in him and he's been tasked with an investigation."

But Ms Alexander told the House of Commons "I do not believe this issue was unavoidable".

More than 300 flights have been cancelled today - including at Heathrow and Gatwick - on top of 1,300 flights from UK airports axed on Tuesday, according to Flightradar24. Tens of thousands of holidaymakers have been left stranded for hours, with distressed passengers reporting being left waiting on runways.

A NATS spokesperson apologised for the delays and advised passengers to check with their airline before travelling to airports.

Mr Rolfe has apologised, telling the BBC that there would be a full investigation into what had gone wrong. Asked about the cause of the problem, Mr Rolfe said a "thorough" investigation would be carried out, but ruled out a cyber-attack.

News.title: UK economy could get £14bn boost by tackling youth employment Neet crisis
News.content:
UK economy could get £14bn boost by tackling youth employment Neet crisis

The hospitality sector is calling on a package of tax cuts from the government to help it get more 'Neets' into work for the first time, which cost boost the economy by more than £14billion

View 3 Images Hotel receptionist Hannah Carolan, 20, spent two years unemployed (Image: Provided)

Tackling a first jobs crisis could give the economy a more than £14billion boost, it is claimed.

‌



Nearly one million young people aged 16 to 24 are classed as Neets - not in employment, education or training, or about one in eight people in that age group. The figure has fallen from the start of 2026 but has risen over the past year.

‌



The Labour government has vowed to find ways to address the problem on the back of final recommendations from former minister Alan Milburn. However, research suggests getting more of the near one million Neets into work could also help grow the UK economy; one of PM Andy Burnham and Chancellor John Healey’s key priorities.

‌



View 3 Images The hospitality sector has appealed to the government for sector specific help to reduce costs to then enable it to take on more young people (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Analysis by hotel chain Hilton and consultants WPI Economics estimates that each Neet who gets a first job generates around £152,000 in economic value per year through higher output, tax revenues, lower benefits spending and reduced long-term scarring effects. Yet many young people struggle to take their first step into work due to a lack of prior experience, leaving them caught in an “experience trap”.

Recent data from the Office for National Statistics showed 400,000 Neets are actively looking for work, yet separate research suggests one in four cite a lack of experience as their biggest barrier to getting a job. WPI calculated that that this “experience trap” could be costing Britain up to £14.4billion a year in lost economic output.

‌



And on Wednesday, Children's Commissioner Rachel De Souza warned that tens of thousands of college teens are hidden from official Neets figures as they only attend for less than half the time. Hilton says it is part of an industry that can help tackle the problem given that hospitality remains one of the industries that offers young people without experience the opportunity to enter the workforce.

View 3 Images Hotel giant Hilton says getting each Neet young person into work is worth £152,000 to the economy (Image: Getty Images)

It, and trade body UKHospitality, are calling for a package of measures from the government specifically targeted at this sector, including reducing employer national insurance contributions, halving hospitality VAT to 10% in line with Europe, and scrapping the proposed holiday tax. Steve Cassidy, senior vice president for Hilton in the UK and Ireland, said: “Hospitality has always been one of the UK’s strongest routes into employment and we see firsthand how taking that first step into work can have a lasting impact on a young person’s confidence, skills and future career prospects.

‌



“This research backs up just how valuable those first-job opportunities continue to be, not only for young people but for the wider economy. Yet too many young people are now caught in an experience trap, unable to get the experience employers are looking for because they cannot access that crucial first opportunity.”

Allen Simpson, chief executive of UKHospitality, said: “The ‘experience trap’ thousands of young people are caught up in is the result of the last two years adding billions of costs onto critical employment sectors like hospitality. Hospitality is the sector of experience and opportunity, regardless of your background, qualifications or circumstances, but the jobs it creates and supports are being taxed out of existence.

"It’s costing the economy and taking away the first step on the career ladder for a whole generation. The benefits of backing hospitality are clear. Billions in economic benefit, opportunities for young people and thousands of people back in work.

Article continues below

"The new Prime Minister should continue to show his support for hospitality, reduce its tax burden and allow the sector to fulfil its potential to drive economic growth and create new jobs in every postcode.”

Hannah Carolan, 20, a receptionist at Hilton London Metropole, got her job after going on the firm's Springboard programme. She said "After leaving college I applied for dozens of jobs but found it difficult to secure interviews. After spending two years unemployed, my confidence began to suffer and I wondered whether I would be able to find a career that was right for me. Employers wanted experience, but I was unable to get a first job that would give me my first taste of work – it was a catch 22.”

News.title: Lawyer who witnessed horrors of 9/11 still providing for victims' families 25 years later
News.content:
Lawyer who witnessed horrors of 9/11 still providing for victims' families 25 years later

EXCLUSIVE: Helping youngsters with scholarships and jobs after witnessing the horrors of 9/11 is part of the vow Michael Barasch made after dozens of firefighters he knew were killed in the horror attacks he witnessed

View 6 Images Michael Barasch - providing jobs and scholarships for relatives of 9/11 victims 25 years on (Image: Ian Vogler / Daily Mirror)

It may be 25 years ago, but the horrific sight of seeing “dozens of people” jumping to their deaths from the World Trade Center is an image that has never left Michael Barasch.

‌



He also personally knew dozens of the firefighters who were killed. And he made a vow that day that whatever he could do to help the families of the victims in the future he would do so. He has certainly kept his promise.

‌



A quarter of a century on, he has given dozens of jobs at his Charitable Foundation to wives, husbands, sons and daughters of those who were died. Just last week another six teenagers, who lives were affected by 9/11, were given scholarships to help with their university fees.

‌



View 6 Images 9/11 - 25 years on Barasch & McGarry Charitable Foundation's still helping victims (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Iconic 9/11 briefcase man vows to never throw it away after World Trade Center horrors 25 years ago READ MORE :

As the victims’ children grew up many were able to seize the opportunity of employment at his offices - just a couple of blocks from the World Trade Centre. "It was the very least I could do,” said Michael, 71.

As we sat in his office he reeled off the names of members of his own staff who had fallen ill in recent years. Secretaries with skin cancer, lawyers with kidney cancer. He has been battling prostate cancer and skin cancer himself. He said: “We’ve given jobs to several dozen children and spouses of those who died on 9/11. It’s been great from a personal point of view and wonderful to help them after what they’ve been through.

‌



"It’s great to help those who are part of the 9/11 community. And they know what it has been like. When people call up to talk about issues surrounding 9/11 and they might say ‘you just don’t know what it’s like’. In fact our people do know exactly what it’s like and that a real help to them.”

View 6 Images Hero firefighter William "Billy" Gormley. (Image: firehero.org)

‌



Michael explained: “They come and perhaps work in the claims department or in various admin jobs. But some fall in love with law and then go off to law school.” He joked: “I tell them ‘I’ve given you a job and now you’re going and leaving me!’ But then some of them actually come back. We’ve got five or six lawyers with us now who all had their first start with us in different roles.”

He added: “It makes me so proud that so many of them end up going on to law school, or it's a way for them to spend some meaningful time giving back in honour of their parents who passed away. It makes me feel great to know that I'm putting my clients at ease, but I'm also giving these young people something meaningful to do with their careers.

“ I'm one of those people who believed the government when they said the air was safe to breathe. It wasn't. My office is three blocks from ground zero. I was exposed to the exact same toxins as the firefighters and cops. And not surprisingly, I got sick like so many others.

‌



"The office workers, the former students, the former teachers, the downtown residents, were all coming down with the same illnesses, the same cancers as the 9/11 heroes. And for me, I had prostate cancer and skin cancer, two of the most common cancers in the 9/11 community.

“Thankfully, both of them were diagnosed early, and that really is the key. I know it sounds corny, but the key to surviving cancer is early detection and early treatment. So I consider myself really lucky."

6 View 6 Images Barasch & McGarry Charitable Foundation's 'Giving Back' event 6 View 6 Images Some of the young scholars who have benefitted from generosity of Barasch & McGarry Charitable Foundation

‌



He heads the Barasch & McGarry charitable foundation. His legal firm represented many firefighters even before 9/11. They hosted an event last week on the 80th floor of 3 World Trade Centre called “Giving Back: Honouring the 25th Remembrance of 9/11”.

He invited the Mirror along to watch as they gave scholarships to Gabriella Abate, Sophia Cucuzza, Ian Dannenfelser, Domenick Masiello, Gianna Romano and Thomas Sheehan. They are all aged just 17 and 18.

Gabriella is honouring her grandad Joseph M Abate senior - a NYPD electrician who restored power at Ground Zero. She will attend Marist University where she study fashion merchandising. Sophia is honouring her mum Jaime Cucuzza who worked at Thomson Reuters downtown office. She will attend Hofstra University to study nursing.

‌



View 6 Images Bridget Gormley who lost her dad Billy to illness caused by 9/11 is one of Michael Barasch's key people (Image: Ian Vogler / Daily Mirror)

Ian is honouring his grandad a lifelong volunteer firefighter and Deputy Chief Marshall with Camden County Fire Marshal’s office. Ian is attending Penn State to study mechanical engineering. Domenick is honouring his grandad Domenick Zernone, a Local 3 electrician who helped restore critical systems after 9/11. He will attend Lafayette College to study mechanical engineering.

Article continues below

Gianna who honouring her granny Marie Erico who worked at Aon’s office in the South Tower. She will attend Penn State to study Communication Sciences and Disorders. Thomas is honouring his mum Delia Tanger who lived in Battery Park and later passed away from cancer. He will attend the New Jersey Institute of Technology.

Among those Michael helped with a job is Bridget Gormley. She lost her dad William “Billy” Gormley a hero firefighter who later died of bladder cancer. She said: “I’ve worked here for eight years. When I first started I was taking phone calls and now I work in a community liaison role.

“Michael likes to help people who can relate to the people he is trying to help. He has absorbed new generation - children who lost their parents at 9/11. People really are very grateful for the opportunities they’ve been given.”

News.title: Anti-migrant protesters targeting Poole RNLI training centre met with heavy police presence
News.content:
Anti-migrant protesters targeting Poole RNLI training centre met with heavy police presence

The latest demo was organised by two groups calling themselves "Poole Patriots" and "Bournemouth Patriots" and comes just days after other high-profile protests in recent days in Dover and Portsmouth

View 6 Images Protesters who turned up outside the RNLI training centre in Poole were met with a heavy police presence (Image: Getty Images)

Anti-migrant activists launched a new protest outside an RNLI centre in Dorset this evening.

‌



Around 60 protesters gathered outside Royal National Lifeboat Institute College in Poole after the event began at around 5pm. The latest demo came just three days after masked protesters abused RNLI heroes in Portsmouth, calling them "collaborators" and "traitors", and just hours after the Prime Minister warned that abuse against the charity's workers would not be tolerated.

‌



There was a heavy police presence at the event on Wednesday night, and private security guards were also seen guarding the RNLI building. Some protesters accused the RNLI of perpetrating criminal activity by helping to bring unvetted young men to the UK. Others handed out rape alarms to women and girls present, telling them "we need to protect ourselves".

‌



View 6 Images Police and private security guards were seen outside the RNLI building (Image: Getty Images)

One protester said: "We are here as a peaceful vigil because of the rape victims, the sexual assault and stab victims, because the RNLI are facilitating bringing these undocumented, unvetted men of fighting age onto our shores. They are coming in boatloads at a time and now further along our coast, which is obviously a problem."

They claimed: "We already have 615 immigrants in our hotels in the Bournemouth area. The RNLI have perpetrated bringing them in as a taxi service, they are perpetrating rapes and criminal activity. Would you leave the front door open to any Tom, Dick and Harry? The answer should be no."

‌



An army veteran, who gave his name as Steve and said he is from the group Hampshire Resistance in Gosport, said: "I'm here because I'm a patriot and I want to help and support other patriots. We are all in this together. We love our country, I served my country. It isn't the RNLI's fault, they're just going by orders. It's a shame because we do need lifeboats, but this is more important to stop this invasion.

View 6 Images A protester speaks on a loud hailer at the protest in Poole (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"I know sometimes what we do isn't going to make an impact, but if we don't protest nobody is going to know there's a problem. The only way to win this is to take back the power and the only way to do that is vote them out. The government is panicking and turning the country into chaos."

Other campaigners spoke through a microphone connected to a speaker calling on the RNLI to stop facilitating the migrants, prompting clapping and cheers from other protesters. One woman said: "It's about what happens afterwards. These men are coming into our communities and the government are handing them pamphlets on how not to rape. They don't live by our rules.

"The left are so righteous. They say we stand for women's rights - no you don't because if you did you would be demanding answers. Every single day there's a rape or a murder. You're forgetting the victims. You think these men on dinghies are the victims - they are not persecuted, they are cowards. If your country is at war you stay and fight for your country, you don't go through 11 countries to get here and leave your women and children behind. They are coming here to fleece us for everything."

‌



View 6 Images Masked anti-migrant protesters gathered in Dover on Saturday

The protest was organised on Facebook by two groups calling themselves "Poole Patriots" and "Bournemouth Patriots". Speaking shortly before the latest protest began on Wednesday afternoon, Andy Burnham's official spokesman said: "Directing abuse at people who dedicate themselves to helping others is appalling. We won't tolerate social media being a haven for this kind of behaviour. We support the police in investigating any threatening or unlawful behaviour and taking action where appropriate."

‌



On Sunday, RNLI heroes in Portsmouth were targeted by far-right thugs for helping to rescue asylum seekers in the English Channel. After helping a dinghy with 120 people on board to safety, they were met by men in a boat shouting: “How do you feel bringing illegal migrants into this country?”

View 6 Images RNLI volunteers were met by shouting protesters as they returned to shore in Porstmouth

A volunteer in a yellow life jacket told them: “I don’t know, I haven’t brought any in.” The protesters replied: “Look at these guys, absolute traitors to this country. Look at the state of you.” Other footage posted also showed people barracking an RNLI crew with calls of “traitors” and “yellowbellies”. Another protester described the lifesavers as “scum”, while some were seen entering the water.

‌



Police are now investigating reports that two RNLI men were later named and pictured online in a social media post by someone calling themselves a "nationalist". Sussex Police said on Wednesday that "investigations are ongoing" into "offensive and threatening commentary" towards RNLI volunteers circulating on social media.

Chief Insp Adam McCaig said: “We would advise anyone considering carrying out any action that could hinder the RNLI's vital lifesaving work to carefully consider the implications. The RNLI exists to save lives at sea, and any disruption to that mission could have serious consequences for those in need of urgent assistance.”

‌



The online poster had written: "We now have names for these two traitors helping 140 asylum seekers into our country last night. We also now have one address that I believe is circulating in Telegram groups." They later added: "Let's make it clear. I don't wish any harm on these two individuals. Their names were posted on X before my post, and I am only reporting what I have seen."

The posts received widespread criticism, including from Hope Not Hate chief executive Nick Lowles, who accused the poster of putting "a target on their backs". RNLI Chief Executive Peter Sparkes also issued a heartfelt statement on Tuesday night pleading for activists not to target the charity. He said: "The RNLI is an apolitical organisation; we are completely independent of government, powered by remarkable, kind people and fuelled by the incredible generosity of the public.

View 6 Images RNLI chief executive Peter Sparkes (Image: RNLI/Nathan Williams)

‌



"For over two hundred years, in all weathers, in peace and war, the RNLI and our amazing volunteers and staff have selflessly dedicated themselves to rescuing people they have never met before, without judgment, fear or favour. When His Majesty’s Coastguard tasks a RNLI lifeboat crew to launch to a vessel or people in distress, whenever and wherever they need us, we will. We will always answer the call, whoever needs our help. It is a legal and moral obligation that our country has, under the United Nations Convention of the Law of the Sea and SOLAS, Safety of Life at Sea. Courage is the RNLI’s currency; dependable, loyal, service to others and our nations is our hallmark."

Mr Sparkes also dismissed false online claims that the RNLI house asylum seekers on their premises or that the organisation performs missions to move migrants to secret locations, which he described as "ludicrous", as well as "completely baseless and untrue". He said: "Recent events have generated deliberate misinformation and a misunderstanding about the RNLI – our purpose, our tasking, and particularly our lifesaving work in the Channel. Sadly, as a result, some of our volunteers and staff have been the subject of online and, in the worst cases, physical abuse.

Article continues below

"The RNLI’s people represent the very best in our society, they selflessly give up their time to keep others safe. Yet they and their families are being threatened by those who would hide behind a balaclava or a keyboard. Their action, in contrast, is wholly unacceptable in a civilised society. We will take whatever steps we can, to care for and protect our people and their families."

Mr Sparkes also attempted to outline facts to fight the fictitious claims being spread online about the RNLI's connection to migrant crossings in the Channel. He added: "RNLI lifeboats were tasked by the coastguard and launched 9,058 times in 2025: 109 of those launches were to those in distress in the Channel, representing 1.2 per cent of the RNLI’s total rescue work.

"Nearly 95 per cent, of those who crossed the English Channel in small boats last year, one of the busiest shipping lanes in the world, were picked up by the UK Border Force. Our mission, and our tasking is to rescue those women, children and men in danger of drowning. Anyone rescued from a small boat by the RNLI is immediately handed over to the UK’s immigration authorities. Illegal immigration is a political issue; the RNLI exists to save lives at sea."

News.title: 'Harry and Meghan risk history repeating dark period for Royals amid tensions with the Firm'
News.content:
'Harry and Meghan risk history repeating dark period for Royals amid tensions with the Firm'

The Duke and Duchess of Sussex have barely been in the country two weeks - creating more questions than answers as to why they here and what their intensions are

View 3 Images Tensions within the Royals after Harry and Meghan's return to the UK risk repeating a dark period of the monarchy's history (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

Leaks, counter leaks and dueling media campaigns between two camps unable to work together. An intense rivalry galvanised by warring courts, unable to pull back from the brink of internal destruction.

‌



Indeed, the War of the Waleses - involving Prince Charles and Princess Diana during the most brutal separation during the 90s - will forever be remembered as one of the most challenging periods for the royal family. And yet, more than 30 years on, history appears to be in danger of repeating itself.

‌



Just two weeks from touching down on British soil - six years after leaving it all behind on the crassly coined ‘Freedom Flight’ - Harry and Meghan have returned to the UK.

‌



View 3 Images Prince Charles and Princess Diana engaged in a brutal briefing war against each other when their marriage broke down (Image: Getty Images)

Should Prince Harry and Meghan Markle stop using their royal titles in public? Take our poll and have your say READ MORE :

Depending on what news outlet you have consumed this week, the sequel that absolutely no one had asked for, will last between six months and 15 years. Best buckle up then!

‌



Apart from the fact, no one quite knows what they are doing here. True enough, Harry may have been homesick. He may have even yearned for the British autumn after what must be an intolerable time in almost constant sunshine on the Californian coast.

Who could really blame him for choosing a quaint British school in the countryside for his children? And maybe, as far fetched as it may sound, Meghan has actually got a job offer with a Netflix smasher.

Yet, none of this has stopped the rumour mill in suggesting the money is running out and they’ve been forced to come back to the drawing board and have another crack at making things work with the family they’ve spent the last six years running roughshod over. The thing is, no one actually knows. It wouldn’t be that surprising even if Harry and Meghan didn’t!

‌



View 3 Images Harry and Meghan have returned to Britain for an "extended stay" according to their team (Image: PA)

The Sussexes' return to Britain has brought more questions than answers. Top of the tree is undoubtedly what do they actually want? Do they, or Harry at least, really want complete reconciliation? Would he even know how to go about it? Developments over the last few weeks would suggest not.

‌



Waiting until three days before global news breaks of your return before telling your dad - the actual King - of your homecoming, might not be considered putting one’s best foot forward. And then we get to the startling coincidences of times gone by.

Barely a fortnight has passed and the briefing wars have begun. The pattern was already so heavily stitched into the fabric of this story, of course, dating back to February 2020.

The terms of their exit was determined by the royal family - only for Harry and Meghan to publish a lengthy statement “clarifying” what the palace had put out just hours earlier. In more recent years there has been a cascade of leaking to journalists on their ‘friendly’ list detailing, to varying levels of dismay, everything from how their children Archie and Lilibet were not invited to the Coronation, to the King no t answering Harry's calls.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

While uncertainty continues to linger in the air, this week the King, through the Lord Chamberlain, got on the front foot by extinguishing any hope the Sussexes may have of coming back to the royal fold. His message, in a letter to local authorities and basically anyone else looking to engage with them, could not have been clearer. They aren't coming back and they don't represent The Firm.

Without drawing breath, Team Sussex draws on the tried and trusted methods of outrage of the past. The letter goes public, the Sussexes relay their dismay, they were “surprised” at the lack of respect. I’ll leave that with you to consider for just a moment.

Article continues below

Get the inside scoop on the monarchy with Mirror Royal WHATSAPP GROUP: Be first to get the biggest royal bombshells and exclusives to your phone by joining our Royal WhatsApp here. We also treat our community members to special offers, promotions, and adverts from us and our partners. If you don’t like our community, you can check out any time you like. If you’re curious, you can read our Privacy Notice. NEWSLETTER: Or sign up to the Mirror's Royal newsletter here to get all the biggest royal news and exclusive pictures, straight to your inbox.

Claim and counter claim reach the public sphere. Harry hasn’t had the decency to call his father - “oh no he has!” the other side cries. Round and round we go.

So where does this leave us, or rather, them? It’s hard to believe it has only been a few weeks since the once considered impossible scenario of repatriation filtered through and then became a reality. It’s going to be a slog to the end of the year if this is a sign of things to come.

News.title: Woman, 26, dead after taxi hits her in Liverpool - heartbroken family pays tribute
News.content:
Woman, 26, dead after taxi hits her in Liverpool - heartbroken family pays tribute

Isobel 'Izzy' Reyland, 26, died after being hit by a private hire taxi on Aigburth Road in Liverpool. Merseyside Police have arrested a 41-year-old man

View 4 Images Isobel "Izzy" Reyland, from south Wales, was hit by a white Toyota Voxy private hire taxi. (Image: Merseyside Police / family handout)

A 26-year-old woman who died after being hit by a taxi in Liverpool was a "funny and loving young lady" who was "living her life to the fullest", her family has said in a heartbreaking tribute.

Isobel "Izzy" Reyland, from south Wales, was hit by a white Toyota Voxy private hire taxi on Aigburth Road at around 5.40pm last Wednesday. She was taken to hospital for treatment but tragically died from her injuries a short time later.

The taxi driver, a 41-year-old man, was arrested on suspicion of causing death by careless or inconsiderate driving while under the influence of drugs. He has since been released under investigation.

Izzy had moved to Liverpool to pursue her career, with her family saying she was "following her dreams" in a city she loved.

View 4 Images Emergency services at the scene after Isobel Reyland was hit by a white Toyota Voxy (Image: Staff Commissioned)

Her family said: "Izzy was a loving and deeply loved daughter, sister, aunty, granddaughter, niece, cousin and sister-in-law who was tragically taken from us far too soon and will be missed beyond words, always.

"She was a beautiful, caring, funny and loving young lady who was following her dreams and her chosen career in a city she loved and living her life to the fullest.

"We are totally devastated and utterly heartbroken as a family at the loss of our darling Izzy. Izzy - you will always be with us and our deepest love for you is everlasting."

It was previously reported that strangers rushed to help Izzy following the crash, with witnesses saying people performed CPR before emergency services arrived.

View 4 Images The fatal crashhappened on the city-bound carriageway of Aigburth Road near Fulwood Road (Image: Staff Commissioned)

Merseyside Police's investigation remains ongoing and officers have appealed for anyone with information to come forward.

Detective Sergeant Andy Roper, from the force's Matrix serious collision investigation unit, previously said: "First and foremost my thoughts and those of my team remain with the woman's family at this sad time. Road death causes devastation for all those involved and it is our absolute priority to get answers for her family.

"An investigation has been launched to ascertain the circumstance of this collision and we are following up a number of lines of enquiry including speaking to potential witnesses and examining CCTV in the area.

View 4 Images Isobel Reyland, 26, was taken to hospital after the crash but died from her injuries a short time later (Image: Staff Commissioned)

"Aigburth Road is a very busy road and we know at that time there would have been a large volume of vehicles including buses, taxis and delivery drivers, together with pedestrians, in the area.

"I would urge anyone who may have witnessed the incident or was travelling in the area at the time with a dashcam fitted to their vehicle to make contact with our team so that we can check if it has captured anything which may provide answers surrounding this collision.

"Also, if you live in the area and have a CCTV system or Ring doorbell, I would be grateful if you could check your footage to see if you captured anything."

A police spokesperson added: "Anyone with information on the incident should contact Merseyside Police serious collision investigation unit on 0151 777 5747 quoting incident reference 26000720150.

Article continues below

"Alternatively, contact the independent charity Crimestoppers anonymously on 0800 555 111, or via their website here: https://crimestoppers-uk.org/give-information/forms/give-information-anonymously In an emergency always call 999."

News.title: Inside Strictly's Karen Hauer's quiet rural life with famous boyfriend and dogs after quitting show
News.content:
When Strictly foxtrots back on to our screens later this month, it will be the first time in 14 years without longest serving female pro dancer Karen Hauer, who shimmied her way through more than 100 numbers on the show. But she’s not ready to kick off her dancing shoes just yet - revealing her ambition to cha-cha her way into the role of fiery Puerto Rican, Anita, in West Side Story. She says: “My dream role would be Anita in West Side Story. The world is my oyster.”

When Strictly’s new season launches on Saturday 19 September, it will also be the first time Karen has watched it live. She says: “I’ve never watched it live - I was always in it.”

And Karen - who announced her departure in a statement on social media in March - is not the only high profile departure. Longtime hosts Claudia Winkleman and Tess Daly have also left, as have pro dancers Gorka Márquez, Nadiya Bychkova, Luba Mushtuk and Michelle Tsiakkas. Karen says: “Things have to evolve. Whether people like it or not.”

But Karen will be rooting for the new hosts, Emma Willis, Josh Widdicombe and Johannes Rabede. She says: “The new series is so exciting. I'll definitely be watching my friends and I'm really looking forward to seeing Johannes, Emma and especially Josh. I danced with him on the Christmas Special dressed as penguins.”

‌



View 5 Images Josh Widdicombe & Karen Hauer perform on the Strictly Christmas special in 2024 (Image: BBC Studios/Guy Levy)

Karen, who was in the show from 2012 to 2025, has already started her new chapter - playing teacher Mavis in Devonshire Park Theatre's production of the Richard Harris comedy, Stepping Out in Eastbourne until the end of April, before taking it on tour until the end of September. She will then be playing the Wicked Queen in Snow White at The Princess Theatre, Torquay, in December and January.

She says: “I’d been preparing myself mentally for a long time to leave [Strictly]. I’m doing great, I’m really happy. I'm going to miss Strictly, but I'm definitely enjoying my new chapter.”

But the dancer was shocked by the outpouring of love she felt from fans when she announced her departure. She says: “I've never felt so much love. I made such an impact without even actually knowing. I was shocked. I was like, ‘how come you guys didn't vote for me to win?’ Goddamn it.”

‌



Giving no dramatic reason for going, she simply says it was “the right time” to go, adding: “There's a time when you just have to go, ‘okay, well, that's a wrap.’ Now I have free time. I don't know what's going to happen in five years. So, I'm literally living the best life that I can right now, and not overthinking about the future.”

View 5 Images Karen Hauer and Simon Davidson, who have been together for around three years (Image: Mike Marsland/Getty Images for Battersea Dogs & Cats Home)

The first to admit to being a romantic, Karen has had three husbands. She was married to dancer Matthew Hauer from 2000 to 2009, to fellow Strictly pro dancer Kevin Clifton from 2015 to 2018 and then to fitness professional Jordan Wyn-Jones from 2022 to 2023.

But she now shares her rural home near Preston, Greater Manchester, with her boyfriend of three years, rugby player Simon Davidson and four rescue dogs, Betty, Phoebe, Marley and Joe. After her hectic Strictly schedule, she says of Simon: “It's probably really weird for him to have me home.”

‌



Positive she has now found ‘The One,’ she continues: “I love love. I think love is incredible, and I found it in Simon. I love being in a partnership, and in a partnership that's healthy. “Knowing what a healthy relationship looks like and being in it … I think that's what I love is, and that's what I've been searching for. Joy for me is being at home with Simon and the dogs.”

Honouring her love of dogs, in November, Karen is hosting the The Burns Bravery Awards, in which the pet nutrition brand is calling on people to nominate Britain's Bravest Dogs. Research from Burns Pet Nutrition reveals that three-quarters of owners say they turn to their dog when they’ve had a bad day.

View 5 Images Honouring her love of dogs, in November, Karen is hosting the The Burns Bravery Awards (Image: Apple Photos Clean Up)

And Karen can see why, saying: “My rescue dogs are the best thing to ever happen to me. Mentally, physically, my dogs get me out of bed, they get me out for a walk. My dogs have been through all my ups and downs. I think my dogs need therapy now.”

‌



The dancer also turns to her mum Mirian when she needs comfort or inspiration. She says: “She inspires me every day. ‘It's not going to be easy, kid, but you got this’ - that's what I've always known since I was a kid. I've always fought and I've seen my mum struggle. I've seen what it takes to make it - not just as a person on television, but to make it in life.

“My mum raised three kids in New York City, in the Bronx, on her own. She always says, ‘don't let your head get to the clouds.’ And that's why I've always been very grounded, no matter what kind of job or who I’ve met. We're all the same. On Strictly, I was never the flashy one, I was always grateful that first of all I had a job - and one that I loved and which entertained the entire nation.”

Karen made it to the Strictly final twice, with partners Jamie Laing and Mark Wright, but never lifted the glitterball. She says: “I was winning every year just being there. It's great getting a 10, it's fantastic, but it's the moments that bring a smile to people’s faces and make them go, ‘That was really funny’, that I’ll remember the most.”

View 5 Images Jamie Laing and Karen Hauer pose up for a Strictly Come Dancing press shot (Image: BBC)

‌



One such moment was when Anton Du Beke and Ann Widdecombe danced together at the Blackpool Tower Ballroom in 2010. This hilarious moment was how she likes to remember the long serving former Conservative MP, who died on July 9, aged 78, and whose death is now the subject of a murder inquiry.

Speaking fondly of Ann and Anton, Karen says: “He took her by the hand and the foot and was just swinging her around in a yellow dress. I was on the floor, peeing myself. It's those moments, that's what Strictly's about.” Meanwhile, Karen gave her many famous Strictly partners - who included Westlife’s Nicky Byrne, actor Greg Wise and comedian Jayde Adams - the same advice.

She says: “I told all of my celebrities, ‘you have to enjoy it. We're going to work hard, but I want to have a laugh. If you're not having a laugh, then this is not going to work.’ A lot of people find it really hard to enjoy it, because there's so much panic.”

Another of Karen’s favourite moments came in 2019, during Halloween week, when her wig came clean off her head on live TV.

‌



“It was hilarious,” says Karen. “But so what if your wig comes off? People are going to remember that you made them smile. That’s what I’ll remember when I’m 85 … or dancing with Jeremy Vine coming out of a bath, or with the late Dave Myers, who I absolutely adored. Wow, I was living the dream, wasn't I?"

*Following a public voting period, winners will be announced at the Burns Bravery Awards in November. For more information, and to nominate your dog, enter at burnspet.co.uk/pages/burns-bravery-awards

News.title: Police launch criminal investigation into Reform UK donations
News.content:
The Metropolitan Police is carrying out a criminal investigation into Reform UK over allegations it broke foreign funding laws, following a broadcast by Channel 4 News last week.

An undercover reporter recorded two senior Reform aides apparently suggesting a way around electoral law to secure foreign party donations, one of which would have totalled Â£500,000.

The police investigation by the Met's Special Enquiry Team is being folded into an inquiry that has been under way into other donations to the party.

A Reform UK spokesman said the party "denies any wrongdoing and will fully cooperate with the investigation".

"We won't be commenting further while a live investigation is under way."

A Met spokesperson said it had received "a number of reports relating to donations and polling involving a political party", after the film by Channel 4 News and Verbatim Investigations was shown on Thursday evening.

In its statement, the Met Police said: "All allegations under investigation relate to potential offences under the Political Parties, Elections and Referendums Act 2000."

"Detectives continue to liaise closely with the Electoral Commission and Crown Prosecution Service as enquiries progress."

The police spokesperson said detectives were seeking to obtain footage relating to the broadcast.

An Electoral Commission spokesperson said the Channel 4 News report included "serious allegations of wrongdoing", adding: "It is right that these are properly and thoroughly investigated by the police.

"In parallel, we are also considering all relevant information and regulatory steps."

The film overshadowed the party's conference in Birmingham and led to the party losing two key figures - Dan Jukes, chief of staff to the leader Nigel Farage, and James Orr, head of policy.

News.title: Air traffic failure was avoidable, says transport secretary
News.content:
A technical failure of the UK's air traffic control system that has caused widespread flight chaos was avoidable, according to the Transport Secretary.

Heidi Alexander told the Commons she had ordered an independent investigation by the aviation watchdog into the system operated by Nats, which went down for four hours on Tuesday.

More than 2,000 flights have been cancelled as disruption continued for a second day with passengers stuggling to fly out of and into the UK.

After meeting with the boss of Nats, Martin Rolfe, Alexander said a cyberattack could be ruled out, but she added: "I do not believe this issue was unavoidable."

Nats has apologised for its third major technical fault in three years.

Alexander said she discussed with Rolfe how Nats, which is 49% owned by the government, "responded to resolve and minimise the disruption as quickly as possible".

She said there had to be "tough questions about resilience of Nats systems", adding: "We also need to think about consumer redress issues."

Earlier on Wednesday the government said it had confidence in Rolfe, who has led Nats for 11 years as airlines such as Wizz Air and Ryanair called for him to step down.

Nats has been asked to investigate the incident and report back in one week. But Alexander said she has also asked the Civil Aviation Authority to conduct an independent review and present an update in six months' time.

Airlines UK, which represents the country's carriers, said it had written to Alexander to "register serious concerns over yesterday's technical failure at Nats - the third major system failure in three years - which has caused major disruption across the UK's aviation network".

Airlines UK's chief executive Tim Alderslade, said: "The result is a system where airlines pick up the bill for the mistakes of others, while the organisations responsible face little or no financial consequence.

"Accountability should sit where responsibility lies and the Civil Aviation Bill offers the opportunity to address this."

The UK Civil Aviation Authority said passengers are unlikely to be entitled to compensation - though it reminded airlines of their responsibilities to look after passengers who flights had been delayed or cancelled.

It added that the disruption caused by the Nats issue is "likely to be considered the result of 'extraordinary circumstances'", meaning passengers "are unlikely to be entitled to compensation for delays or cancellations that were directly caused by the incident."

News.title: National security can't come at expense of social security, Burnham says
News.content:
In the Commons session, Burnham repeated that the government would meet the Nato target of spending 3.5% of GDP on defence by 2035, with a target date for hitting the 3% figure set out in the spending review in the spring.

The PM said he had appointed John Healey, who resigned as Sir Keir Starmer's defence secretary over the government's failure to commit to a 3% increase by 2030, "because of his strong commitment to the defence of this nation".

However, Badenoch hit back that 2035 was "a decade away" and "the threats are now".

She questioned whether Burnham was "unable" or "just unwilling" to meet the 2030 target.

In response, Burnham insisted: "This chancellor of all chancellors will be willing to provide that funding to our armed forces."

However, he rejected a Conservative plan to partly fund increased defence spending by saving at least Â£4bn through reforms to housing benefit.

"I don't think, myself, that taking Â£4bn out of housing benefit is going to get the right consensus around this issue because that would create levels of homelessness in this country... that we wouldn't have seen before, hundreds of thousands of children in temporary accommodation," he said.

"Yes, we do everything to support our national security, but it can't come at the expense of social security."

He added: "This side of the House will not be forced to choose between the two and we will set out a plan to get to 3.5% by 2035 at the spending review."

Badenoch said Burnham's comments were "unbelievable", adding: "We need to fund our defence, not spend all of our money on welfare."

Burnham insisted he would "bring the welfare budget down" by tackling the number of young people not in education, employment or training.

"That's the Labour way to get the welfare bill down," he said.

"That is the right way to fund defence."

Badenoch accused Burnham of being "continuity Keir".

"He's pretending that he's the change candidate. But the fact is, he's still failing to cut welfare," she said.

As prime minister, Sir Keir attempted to cut disability benefits but was forced to row back on the plans in the face of opposition from Labour MPs.

Cutting the welfare bill is a key part of Tory proposals for funding increased defence spending.

Spending on benefits has ballooned in recent years and is forecast to rise to Â£408.6bn in 2030/31, according to figures from the Department for Work and Pensions.

There is particular concern about the nearly one million young people in the UK who are not in education, employment or training â known as "Neets".

The government has asked former minister Alan Milburn to look into the issue and he is expected to publish his final recommendations for how to tackle the problem shortly.

News.title: Miliband rejects chief rabbi's claim British Jews in greater danger after sanctions move
News.content:
Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband has rejected the chief rabbi's warning that British Jews are at greater risk after the UK announced sanctions on Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank.

Miliband said that as a "proud British Jew" he disagreed with UK Chief Rabbi Sir Ephraim Mirvis, who described the move as a "truly dark day" that would "succeed only in bolstering the very extremism they seek to target".

"We all need to do more to tackle antisemitism," Miliband said, "but I believe we can do that and stand up for British values".

The sanctions on trade with illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank come against a backdrop of rising antisemitic incidents across the UK.

The Community Security Trust (CST), an organisation that provides security support to the Jewish community, recorded 1,926 incidents of anti-Jewish hate across the UK in the first six months of 2026, a 21% increase on the same period in 2025.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham defended his government's decision, telling MPs that "Britain has to stand for fairness against injustice".

"Where people are being bullied out of their homes... we will always stand with the underdog," he said.

The Palestinian presidency welcomed the UK's decision, saying it was "an important step towards confronting Israel's colonial system and its violations against the Palestinian people".

There has been mixed reaction within the UK Jewish community on the sanctions and possible implications for security.

The chief rabbi called the government's announcement "little more than political flag bearing for mendacious anti-Israel rhetoric".

Sir Ephraim said: "Gesture politics of this kind feeds into an increasingly hostile discourse about Israel, and the cumulative effect of such punitive policies is to further embolden those, at home and abroad, who use hatred as a weapon against Jews."

Asked about Mirvis's comments, Miliband said: "I don't agree with the chief rabbi, somebody... of whom I have great respect."

He told BBC Radio 4's Today programme that "anyone who holds British Jews - or indeed Jews around the world - responsible for the actions of the Israeli government, is engaging in antisemitism, pure and simple".

Meanwhile, the Jewish Leadership Council (JLC) warned the government's decision "risks becoming a de facto boycott of Israel" and accused Miliband of "yielding to pressure from the most extreme elements of British society".

The Board of Deputies of British Jews said the decision to make the announcement before Rosh Hashanah - the Jewish New Year festival which begins on Friday - brings "concerns for communal security at their highest levels... felt particularly acutely by British Jews".

It added that the deteriorating relationship between the UK and Israel has the potential to "further inflame community tensions here too", while also noting it had warned the Israeli government over the "intolerable settler violence" that harms Israel's reputation.

Greater Manchester Police (GMP) announced on Wednesday that extra resources would be allocated during the Jewish High Holy Days to provide "extra visibility and security" and "ensure everyone can celebrate this time safely".

Ch Supt Dave Meeney said: "Our officers will continue working with Jewish communities as we head into this important period for their faith, which we understand is a time which may bring heightened concern for the community."

News.title: RNLI volunteer targeted online and branded 'traitor' after Portsmouth protests
News.content:
An RNLI volunteer who was targeted with abuse online after being wrongly identified as having helped small boat migrants reach land in Portsmouth has told BBC Verify he is not a "traitor".

Neil and his colleagues were filmed wearing their lifesaving gear on a lifeboat by anti-migrant activists near the harbour on Sunday night, after hundreds of protesters descended on the area and shut down roads in response to dozens of asylum seekers being brought to shore.

The lifeboat crew's images were later used in posts accusing them of assisting what some users on X described as "an invasion", several of which also called for them to be "named and shamed".

These posts, which were collectively viewed at least two million times, also incorrectly claimed Neil and another colleague were two entirely different RNLI crew members whose names were available online.

News.title: BBC drops Drag Race UK after eight series
News.content:
RuPaul's Drag Race UK is leaving the BBC after eight series, the broadcaster has confirmed.

A spokesperson for the channel said it was facing "very difficult choices" in the face of "significant financial pressures".

The show is currently broadcast on BBC Three and iPlayer. Future series - as well as its spin-off vs The World - will be broadcast on Wow Presents Plus, a streaming platform owned by the production company behind the show.

At its peak, the UK version of the international drag competition averaged at around 1.5 million viewers per episode.

A spokesperson for the BBC said it was "proud [...] of this groundbreaking show" and thanked "RuPaul, World of Wonder and everyone involved, both on and off screen".

Started in 2019, Drag Race UK brought British drag into mainstream entertainment in the UK, and has made household names of drag performers such as La Voix, Danny Beard, and Tia Kofi.

The show sees drag queens compete in a series of challenges to impress judges RuPaul, Michelle Visage, Graham Norton and Alan Carr, and often features big name celebrity guest judges.

It has become a staple of LGBTQ+ culture and has been praised for its portrayal of the distinct style of British drag.

The corporation is currently rolling out plans to make Â£500m of savings, with director-general Matt Brittin previously telling staff "the scale of savings requires tough choices".

A BBC spokesperson said: "As the BBC continues to navigate significant financial pressures and deliver the savings required of us, we have had to make some very difficult choices, none of which have been taken lightly."

Announcing the news on Instagram, Wow Presents Plus said a "new era" of Drag Race UK was on the way.

A new series, Drag Race UK All Stars, which sees previous fan favourites return to compete again, will premier in Autumn 2027 exclusively on Wow Presents Plus.

BBC News understands the current series of Drag Race UK, which launched in September 2026, will continue to air as normal on BBC Three and appear on iPlayer, and all existing series will continue to be available once the move is complete.

The BBC declined to comment on whether future series of other international versions of the show, including Drag Race Canada and Drag Race Down Under, would continue to air.

Earlier this year, the BBC announced it was dropping LGBTQ+ dating show I Kissed a Boy - which made history as the UK's first gay dating show - and I Kissed a Girl.

Jordan Burrow, a contestant on series two of I Kissed a Boy, said the decision was an example of "where we're at within the queer community".

The corporation said at the time that it was "exceptionally proud" of the shows but they had to make "difficult choices in light of our funding challenges".

News.title: Apple's new boss starts with big gamble on costly first folding iPhone
News.content:
John Ternus has entered his second week as Apple's chief executive and the company has revealed the first major change to the iPhone since it was released almost 20 years ago.

Ternus, who took on Apple's top job after Tim Cook stepped down, was onstage on Wednesday at the company's annual product release event in front of huge images of the first foldable iPhone.

With a book-style format, the new iPhone, dubbed the Duo, is the largest ever size of the product. And with a US starting price of $1,999 (Â£1,475) going up to $3,200, it is also the most expensive. UK prices start at Â£1,999.

Ternus said the Duo was "inspired by the iPad" but called the folding features "fluid and completely intuitive."

The foldable phone has been a work-in-progress inside Apple for several years.

When unfolded, the new Duo has the look of a small iPad. When folded in half, it has the look of a wider iPhone.

Ternus said during the event that Apple wanted to avoid the look and feel of other foldable smart phones on the market, which he said "feel like two phones stuck together... making a larger screen feel much smaller."

The Duo, he said, is the "result of a series of remarkable innovations that we think will redefine the experience of using a foldable phone."

Ternus was directly involved in developing the foldable iPhone as he spent many years as a top executive inside Apple's hardware division before being tapped earlier this year as Cook's successor.

News.title: Hundreds mourn police officer killed in wrong-way A66 crash
News.content:
Hundreds have turned out for the funeral of one of the police officers killed in a wrong-way crash.

PC Matthew Blades, 37, and PC Tom Clough, 38, died when a Volkswagen Passat collided with their marked armed response car on the A66 at South Bank, near Middlesbrough, on 22 August. Five young men were also killed.

A full ceremonial police funeral took place for PC Blades in Hartlepool earlier, with hundreds of officers from Cleveland and forces across the country lining the street in a guard of honour.

Speaking on behalf of his family, Cleveland Police Federation chair Lauren Somerville said "life feels unbearably quiet" without the father-of-two's "silly jokes" and laughter.

Members of other emergency services were present at St Joseph's Roman Catholic Church, alongside community leaders and politicians.

Cleveland Police chief constable Victoria Fuller greeted mourners at the entrance to the church.

Policing minister Sarah Jones and Home Office minister Anna Turley also attended.

News.title: Man charged with assisting Russian intelligence service
News.content:
A 31-year-old British man has been charged under the National Security Act over alleged contact with Russia's military intelligence agency.

Joshua Cammidge, from Swindon, allegedly received instructions from an individual believed to be linked to the GRU Volunteer Corps, a group controlled by Russia's military intelligence agency, the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) said.

He has been charged with assisting a foreign intelligence service and preparatory conduct.

He is due to appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court on Thursday.

Cammidge was arrested at an address in Swindon on Friday by Counter Terrorism Policing (CTP) London officers, supported by officers from Wiltshire Police.

He was taken to a London police station and searches were carried out at a different address in Swindon, the Metropolitan Police said.

He was further arrested and detained under the National Security Act on Saturday.

The force said he has been charged with assisting a foreign intelligence service contrary to Section 3 of the National Security Act 203 and preparatory conduct contrary to Section 18 of the National Security Act 2023.

Frank Ferguson, chief crown prosecutor for the CPS's Special Crime and Counter Terrorism Division, said: "Our prosecutors have worked to establish that there is sufficient evidence to bring the case to court and that it is in the public interest to pursue criminal proceedings.

"We remind all concerned that proceedings against the defendant are active and he has the right to a fair trial.

"It is vital that there should be no reporting, commentary or sharing of information online which could in anyway prejudice these proceedings."

Security Minister Dan Jarvis said: "The police have taken action against a potential threat, and I thank them for the vital work they do every day to keep us safe.

"Whilst it would be inappropriate to comment further on the specifics of this case, I know people will be concerned about recent incidents across Europe, intended to sow fear, create disruption and undermine support for Ukraine. They will not succeed."

News.title: Drug gangs exploited and raped us as teens, then police failed us, women tell BBC
News.content:
Warning: Contains details of sexual exploitation

"It was the thrill of being with a bad boy."

Christine was 13 when she began exchanging messages online with someone she believed was a teenage boy.

On their first meeting, she discovered he was a grown man 10 years older than herself. He also told her he was involved with gangs and drugs.

"I always knew, OK, he's probably hurt someone, but in terms of hurting me, I didn't think it would get to that point," she says.

Over the next few years, he would use Christine to courier drugs, subject her to extreme sexual exploitation, and assault her so violently she feared she might die.

Christine is one of four women who have chosen to waive their anonymity and speak publicly to the BBC documentary, Britain's Forgotten Girls, about how they were targeted by criminals when they were children.

Their stories, covering 2002 to last year, differ in detail - but reveal strikingly similar patterns of abuse. All four describe being targeted by boys and older men connected to drug gangs, manipulated into abusive relationships, then repeatedly sexually exploited.

All believe the authorities failed to protect them and did not take their allegations seriously.

The sexual and criminal exploitation of girls by drug gangs has long been overshadowed in public discussion by the focus on sexual grooming gangs, according to front-line social workers and experts in the field.

"For grooming gangs, the primary purpose is often the sexual exploitation of those girls, but the primary purpose of a drug gang is to make money off selling drugs and other criminal activity," says Connie Muttock from the children's charity, Centre for Young Lives.

Girls are brought in to generate money, says Muttock, but many are also sexually abused by gang members.

News.title: Learner drivers still forced to wait months to book tests
News.content:
Learner drivers have to wait an average 20 weeks, or around five months, before booking a practical test, according to new figures, despite attempts to reduce delays.

The data from the Driver and Vehicle Standards Agency (DVSA) for August is only a marginal improvement from 20.2 weeks in July.

The average wait time between booking and sitting a test is unchanged at 11.1 weeks.

The DVSA initially had a target of reducing the average waiting time to seven weeks by the end of last year. Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander pushed the target back to summer 2026, but subsequently admitted even that would not be possible.

The DVSA made a number of changes to its practical driving test booking system earlier this year.

Only the learner driver themself is now able to book their driving test, blocking an instructor or third parties from booking using the learner's details.

There is also a geographical restriction which means a learner can only book a test at their three local test centres, rather than one at the other side of the country if they found a test available.

The number of times a would-be driver can swap a test date has also been restricted.

News.title: Divorcing abusive husband cost woman £105k
News.content:
A woman who endured years of abusive controlling behaviour by her ex-husband says it has cost her more than Â£105,000 to divorce him.

Annabelle Boucher, 48, from Somerset, wants the law changed after she paid Â£75,000 to David Rogers, 61, despite him admitting to coercive and controlling behaviour. She also had to pay her legal costs.

"I thought being stuck in this relationship I couldn't get out of would be highlighted within the divorce procedure," Boucher said. "But the divorce law doesn't take into account the fact that he was a criminal."

The Ministry of Justice (MoJ) said it had begun a consultation to reform the law so "family courts meet the needs of domestic abuse victims".

Boucher, a mother from Chiselborough, said Rogers had come into her life in "a whirlwind" in 2017 and the pair got married two years later.

It was once they were married that things started to "take a turn", she said, and "some very extreme behaviour started to happen".

"It creeps up on you and you're in it, and so you don't kind of notice what is happening."

Boucher said she had ended up "shutting down emotionally" and "cutting off from everyone" because she feared what would happen.

"You find that you're trapped within a situation that you can't get out of."

News.title: Channel 4 to cut 340 jobs by the end of the year in major shake-up
News.content:
Channel 4 has said it plans to cut 340 jobs before the end of the year, reducing its workforce by more than a quarter.

The network, which broadcasts Gogglebox and The Great British Bake Off, will lose around 28% of its current 1,270 staff following a strategic review of the organisation.

Priya Dogra, Channel 4's chief executive, said the announcement "marks the first phase of our transformation, ensuring Channel 4 is the right shape and size to deliver its future strategy and focus investment in the programmes audiences love".

Caroline Dinenage, chair of the culture, media and sport committee said the news would be "deeply worrying for the talented and dedicated people who work at Channel 4".

The network said it planned to focus on creating a simpler and more efficient operating model and enable greater investment in distinctive programming.

In her statement, Dogra said: "Channel 4 is a precious asset which plays a unique role in the UK.

"We need to secure and own our future so we can continue to make shows others won't, reach audiences others can't, and thrive as a distinctive and disruptive British voice for future generations.

"The challenges we face require a fundamental transformation in how we work. I know the proposals we are announcing today will be very difficult for many colleagues and will have a significant impact across the organisation."

She added: "These decisions have not been taken lightly, but I strongly believe they are necessary to create a simpler, more focused and more sustainable Channel 4."

News.title: Home with hundreds of thousands of cockroaches like a horror movie, pest controller says
News.content:
Hundreds of thousands of cockroaches were found in a shared home in an infestation described as the worst the pest controller had seen in 38 years.

Gareth Davies, who said the scene had looked like one from a "Stephen King film", said his team had used specialist equipment to vacuum up "hundreds of thousands" of cockroaches from the four bedroom property in Pontypridd, south Wales.

He said his company had dealt with hundreds of cockroach jobs in the past 12 months, compared with just a handful a year five years ago.

There have been reports of a rise in cockroach sightings across some of Britain's urban areas, according to the British Pest Control Association (BPCA).

The recent warmer weather is thought by some experts to be speeding up cockroaches' breeding cycle.

News.title: Man shot by police after woman stabbed at property
News.content:
A man has been shot by police after a woman was stabbed at a property in Luton.

Shots were fired by armed officers at an address in Cardigan Street at about 12:50 BST on Tuesday.

The man was struck in the arm and leg after a Bedfordshire Police officer discharged four shots, while another fired a baton round.

The Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) said it was now investigating the police response.

"We have secured the police firearms for examination and CCTV and officers' body worn video have been viewed," a spokesman said.

The man's injuries were described as life-changing but not life-threatening.

Both he and the woman, whose injuries were also not life-threatening, were taken to hospital for treatment.

Bedfordshire Police said it was responding to reports that a man was threatening a woman with a knife at the address.

Det Ch Supt Zara Brown said officers "responded quickly" to the unfolding incident.

"As part of this response, shots were fired by police, and one man sustained serious injuries," she continued.

"Immediate first aid was provided, and he has been taken to hospital, where he remains under police watch."

The force pledged to provide further information about the IOPC investigation when possible.

News.title: Shane Richie pleads not guilty to drink-driving
News.content:
EastEnders actor Shane Richie has pleaded not guilty to a single charge of drink-driving.

The 62-year-old, who has played Alfie Moon in the BBC soap on and off since 2002, was arrested at a petrol station in Harlow, Essex, on 29 July where he was with his Hyundai IX35.

Richie, from Tadworth in Surrey, has appeared at Colchester Magistrates' Court via video link from a hotel room.

The actor - who appeared under his real name of Shane Roche - spoke only to confirm his name, address and plea. He is next due to appear for trial at the same court on 17 November 2027.

News.content:

President George W. Bush was jogging around a Florida golf course before dawn when I first saw him on September 11, 2001.

As one of two Reuters correspondents traveling with Bush that day, I was covering what was expected to be a routine event with schoolchildren to promote his education policies. He had been president of the United States less than eight months.

Within hours, the untested Bush was confronting the worst attack on American soil since Pearl Harbor in 1941.

The tragedy unfolded as Bush visited the Emma E. Booker Elementary School in Sarasota, Florida. As the president was meeting staff and students, I was in a nearby press center set up for reporters. We watched a live television broadcast showing smoke pouring from one of the World Trade Center twin towers in New York. It had been hit by a plane in what we initially assumed was an accident. Then, as we watched, a second plane struck.

open image in gallery President George W. Bush at his early morning school reading event as he was interrupted by his Chief of Staff Andrew Card ( AFP via Getty Images )

Bush was at the school, reading to children. Cameras captured the shocked look on his face as a White House aide entered the classroom and whispered to him about the second plane, saying "America is under attack."

By the end of the week, Bush would show a range of emotions as he came to grips with events that marked a turning point in his presidency and in American life — horror and anger at the attacks, grief and tears for the victims, and defiant promises to make those responsible pay.

The former president, now 80, plans to attend a ceremony on Friday to mark the 25th anniversary of the attacks at Ground Zero in New York. On Wednesday evening, he will share his reflections on the anniversary at his presidential library in Dallas, while 16 artworks he has painted reflecting the courage and sacrifice of that day will be on display.

"It became evident ... that the world had changed," Bush would later tell CBS's 60 Minutes II.

open image in gallery Bush makes a telephone call as White House Director Of Communications Dan Bartlett points to footage of the attack on the World Trade Center from Emma Booker Elementary School on Sept. 11, 2001 ( Getty Images )

Bush spent the rest of his presidency working to prevent another such attack. The hijackings exposed security vulnerabilities, spurring increased safety measures at airports and public buildings. His administration drew fire for the harsh interrogation tactics used on some Islamic militant suspects, and his 2003 invasion of Iraq was seen by many as a costly mistake.

The former president declined an interview request from Reuters for this story.

Scrambling to protect the president

A quarter century later, the memories remain vivid.

In the immediate aftermath of the hijacked plane attacks, there was a scramble to protect the president. As Bush was whisked away to Air Force One to leave Florida, the scale of the crisis was becoming clear.

The World Trade Center towers collapsed, leading to the deaths of about 3,000 people. A third plane plowed into the Pentagon, killing 64 people on the plane and 125 in the building. A fourth plane slammed into a field in Shanksville, Pennsylvania, after passengers fought back against the hijackers, and all 44 people on board died.

open image in gallery Bush speaks to Vice President Dick Cheney by phone aboard Air Force One on Sept. 11, 2001 ( Getty Images )

Panic gripped Washington. Plumes of smoke from the Pentagon prompted fears of car bombs. The White House was evacuated, with the Secret Service telling female staffers to take off their heels and run.

Bush spent the day flying across the country on Air Force One, first to Barksdale Air Force Base in Louisiana and then to Offutt Air Force Base in Nebraska. Later, he was to push for improved communications equipment on Air Force One after he had trouble staying in touch with the White House as he flew around the country.

In Nebraska, he entered an underground bunker to hold a teleconference briefing with top national security aides and Vice President Dick Cheney.

Eager to return to Washington, Bush arrived back at the White House late that afternoon. That night he gave an Oval Office address.

"The pictures of airplanes flying into buildings, fires burning, huge structures collapsing, have filled us with disbelief, terrible sadness, and a quiet, unyielding anger," Bush said.

open image in gallery Reuters Correspondent Steve Holland was with Bush that day to cover a routine school reading event ( REUTERS )

Meanwhile, along with much of the White House press corps, I was still stranded in Florida, unable to fly anywhere as all air travel had been shut down. As president of the White House Correspondents' Association at the time, I helped push for our return home, and we finally took a chartered bus back to the capital.

After a 14-hour drive, our first view of Washington was the smoking gash in the Pentagon.

On September 14, I traveled with Bush to Ground Zero. The towers were still burning, the smell evident miles away. As Bush walked around the ravaged site with then-Mayor Rudy Giuliani, there were worries that some surrounding buildings had weakened to the point of collapse.

A thick layer of ash lay everywhere, on sidewalks, streets and on the shoulders of weary firefighters.

open image in gallery Shoes belonging to Holland that he wore at Ground Zero during a media tour with Bush on Sept. 14, 2001 ( REUTERS )

Standing on the remains of a firetruck, Bush told emergency crews that the United States was now at war with Islamic militants.

"I can hear you! I can hear you! The rest of the world hears you! And the people who knocked these buildings down will hear all of us soon!" he said through a bullhorn.

The shoes I wore that day were covered with ash and soot. When I got back home, I put them in a plastic bag and stowed them in a closet.

Twenty-five years later, there they remain. Too ruined to wear, too dear to throw away.
