Donald Trump has raised questions over the timing of a UK ban targeting trade with illegal Israeli settlements in the West Bank.

Yet the US president seemed unusually hesitant to elaborate on the joint sanctions from Britain, Canada and France, stating he wished to consult Israel first to "find out their thinking".

Announced by Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband on Tuesday, the policy has provoked a diplomatic dispute with Benjamin Netanyahu’s government alongside domestic criticism.

Asked about the trade ban as he headed to a Republican convention in Texas, Mr Trump said: “Well, I’ve just seen it and I’ll be speaking to Israel. I’ll be speaking to them and I’ll find out what’s their thinking.

open image in gallery Trump has raised questions over the timing of a UK ban ( AFP/Getty )

“I understand exactly what’s going on, but I want to find out why all of a sudden does that happen.”

It comes as the majority of people in Britain support the government’s decision to prohibit imports from Israeli settlements in the West Bank, according to fresh polling.

The snap YouGov survey, carried out on Wednesday, found that 52 per cent of respondents back the trade restrictions announced by foreign secretary Ed Miliband as Labour delivers on its pledge to adopt a firmer stance regarding Gaza.

Of the 4,506 British adults polled, a third (33 per cent) said they "completely approve" of the ban, alongside 19 per cent who stated they "somewhat approve".

open image in gallery Burnham defended the sanctions in the Commons during Prime Minister’s Questions on Wednesday ( PA )

By contrast, only 17 per cent voiced opposition — 10 per cent saying they "completely" opposed the measure and 7 per cent indicating they were "somewhat" against it — while 31 per cent said they did not know.

Prime minister Andy Burnham defended the sanctions in the Commons during Prime Minister’s Questions on Wednesday.

"In this difficult and dangerous world, Britain has to stand for something," Mr Burnham told the Commons on Wednesday. "Britain has to show leadership, Britain has to stand for fairness against injustice."

The measures restrict the import of settlement-produced goods, impose financial sanctions on developers, and halt arms export licences contributing to the occupation.

The move comes amid heightening international backlash surrounding Israel’s controversial plans for further development in the E1 corridor.

Construction in E1 severs the northern and southern West Bank from East Jerusalem, rendering a contiguous two-state solution geographically impossible.

Under international law, all Israeli settlements in the occupied territories are considered illegal — a stance that was reaffirmed by the International Court of Justice in July 2024.

President Donald Trump said he expects the war with Iran to end “immediately” after the November midterm elections, claiming Tehran is trying to influence the vote by prolonging the conflict.

Trump, 80, made the comments to reporters at Joint Base Andrews Wednesday before boarding the new Qatari-gifted Air Force One for Dallas, where he is attending the Republican Party’s first national midterm convention. His departure was delayed after an emergency slide deployed on the aircraft and had to be checked before he boarded.

“I think the war will end immediately after the election because they can't hold out any longer,” Trump told reporters. “They're desperate to try and affect the election, so that we can get a nice, weak group of people in there and leave them alone and let them have their nuclear weapon.”

Polling has shown America is not thrilled with the war, and its approval ratings have dropped as it has dragged on. The figures could hurt Republicans at the polls in the midterm elections if it continues to drag on and America disapproves. A recent NBC News poll found just 31 percent of Americans approve of his handling of the war.

open image in gallery President Donald Trump said he expects the war with Iran to end ‘immediately’ after the midterm elections because ‘they can't hold out any longer’ ( Reuters )

Trump also argued that Iran’s goal is to obtain a nuclear weapon, warning of the consequences if Tehran, the capital of Iran, were to acquire one.

“All they want is a nuclear weapon, and if they had a nuclear weapon, the whole world is in deep trouble,” he added.

The president did not provide a specific reason for why he believes Iran will end the conflict immediately after the election. He has previously said the U.S. military operation would not become a prolonged war.

On Friday, Trump said the conflict with Iran was “small potatoes” and defended Vice President JD Vance’s description of the fighting as not a “war.” Vance said Thursday that there was no active shooting at the time, despite ongoing tensions and recent Iranian attacks.

Trump’s latest comments came as the conflict entered its seventh month and fighting around the Strait of Hormuz intensified.

Iran said Wednesday it attacked 10 ships near the Strait of Hormuz after the U.S. sank five Iranian tankers, escalating tensions and sending oil prices above $100 a barrel for the first time since July.

The increase has contributed to higher gasoline and diesel prices in the U.S., adding to concerns about inflation and household costs.

open image in gallery Iran said Wednesday it attacked 10 ships near the Strait of Hormuz after the U sank five Iranian tankers, pushing oil prices above $100 a barrel ( AFP/Getty )

Trump said Wednesday that he expects oil prices to fall after the midterms, once the war ends. He also acknowledged that negotiations with Iran remain possible, although he said diplomacy is not currently something his administration is pursuing.

“Right after the election, oil prices are going to be tumbling downward,” Trump said, the Associated Press reported. “I think it’s going to take a little bit longer than the midterm.

The comments come as Republicans gather in Dallas for the two-day midterm convention, which is focused heavily on Trump and his record ahead of the November 3 elections. Trump is scheduled to speak at the convention, along with Vance and other Republican leaders.

The Independent has contacted the White House for comment.

News.title: Liverpool v Atletico Madrid LIVE: Mac Allister scores stunner but Barcola limps off injured

An emergency inflatable slide deployed from Air Force One Wednesday afternoon as President Donald Trump waited to board the aircraft at Joint Base Andrews to travel to the Republican midterm convention in Dallas, Texas.

At about 2:20 p.m., the slide rolled out onto the tarmac from the right side of the Qatari-gifted aircraft, opposite the side typically used by Trump to board, according to a White House pool report. Trump was seated nearby on Marine One at the time.

The president told reporters that “they were doing a check on the slide,” which he said “takes about 15 minutes.” Asked by a reporter whether he’s sure that the aircraft is safe to fly, Trump replied: “Yeah, I am, or I wouldn’t be on it.”

The slide was later deflated and transported away, and the jet then took off.

The new Air Force One, a $400 million Boeing 747‑8, was gifted to Trump by Qatar’s royal family last year. After Pentagon-led modifications, the plane was rushed into presidential service this summer as a temporary replacement for the aging aircraft traditionally used to transport the president. Trump made his inaugural flight aboard the aircraft in July.

open image in gallery An emergency inflatable slide deployed from Air Force One at Joint Base Andrews on Wednesday as President Donald Trump waited to travel to the Republican midterm convention in Dallas ( Getty Images )

open image in gallery The president told reporters that ‘they were doing a check on the slide,’ which he said ‘takes about 15 minutes’ ( AP )

In addition to the controversy over the lavish gift — reportedly one Trump plans to keep after leaving office — there have been questions about the plane’s security.

In July, Trump switched aircraft while leaving a NATO summit in Turkey after U.S. officials received intelligence of a potential Iranian assassination threat. On July 8, Trump publicly boarded the older Air Force One rather than the new, Qatari-gifted jet he had flown in on.

According to The New York Times, the Secret Service urged the president not to use the new aircraft for the departure from Turkey, with sources telling the outlet that it lacked certain security features present on the older plane.

A White House spokesperson pushed back, telling the Times: “The new Air Force One is a state-of-the-art aircraft that has been fitted with high-level security protocols that ensure the safety of the president and his staff.”

open image in gallery Trump speaks to reporters before boarding Air Force One at Joint Base Andrews in Maryland on September 9 ( AFP/Getty )

It was later reported that — as part of a covert security operation —Trump was moved into a catering cart and secretly flown out of Turkey on a different military aircraft, while other staffers and reporters remained aboard the older Air Force One.

After the July trip, Trump said that the $400 million aircraft would be taken out of service and “maxed out” with additional security upgrades.

However, a senior White House official told The Independent last week that Trump plans to use the Qatari-gifted jet for his trip to Ireland September 12.

The Independent has contacted the White House for comment.

Andy Burnham has recognised "risks to national security" posed by artificial intelligence, as a prominent safety researcher at Anthropic suggested the technology could destroy humanity over the coming decade.

The Prime Minister was questioned in the Commons regarding the potential hazards of AI after Evan Hubinger cautioned he believed there was a greater than 10 per cent probability of a species-ending threat within 10 years.

This follows reports in the Financial Times that US firm Anthropic withheld its newest model from the UK’s AI Safety Institute, one of the premier global bodies for evaluating the technology’s risks.

Asked about the report by Liberal Democrat leader Sir Ed Davey during Prime Minister’s Questions, Mr Burnham said: “He is absolutely right that AI poses risks to our national security, but it also could be the source of solutions to keeping us safer.”

“The offer is open to colleagues on all sides of the House to be part of that crucial discussion,” he said.

Burnham spoke out after Hubinger’s comments on AI ( PA )

Earlier on Wednesday, Mr Hubinger laid out his concerns about the potential advancement of AI in a post on social media.

“We really do earnestly believe AI could kill all humans! I personally think it is >10% within the next decade. I believe Anthropic is trying its best, but we do not yet have a plan to solve alignment for superintelligence and are not clearly on track to,” he wrote on X.

His post came in response to another Anthropic researcher, Jacob Coxon, warning that a race between companies towards self-improving superintelligence was “gambling with our lives”, as he resigned from his role at the firm.

Announcing his departure, Mr Coxon said that Anthropic and OpenAI, its main competitor, were not “acting responsibly” and that people outside of AI labs were underestimating the power of the technology.

“The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade. This is not a marketing stunt,” he said.

Andy Burnham acknowledged “risks to national security” posed by artificial intelligence as a top safety researcher at Anthropic suggested the technology could wipe out humanity in the next decade.

“No other human activity poses this level of danger.”

Former Cabinet Office minister Darren Jones called for a new multi-national treaty to regulate the development of the technology after the researchers’ warnings.

In a letter to the Prime Minister, UN secretary general Antonio Guterres and OECD secretary general Mathias Cormann, he wrote: “The debate ranges from the end of humanity to claims of ‘marketing hype’ pre-IPO. Either way, governments must now step in.

“We need a new multi-national treaty for the regulated and safe development of superintelligence.

“Not a ban on innovation or scientific endeavour, but a safety first approach to the rapid development of this technology.”

A Cabinet Office spokesperson said: “The UK is a world leader in AI security and we have the best-funded, best-resourced security institute globally.

“The AI Security Institute continues to collaborate closely with industry partners, including Anthropic, to make models safer. Only last week it tested OpenAI’s most powerful model GPT-6 Astra before public release.

“These risks do not stop at national borders and no country can tackle them alone. The UK will continue to test the most advanced models, build a rigorous scientific understanding of their capabilities and risks, and ensure policy decisions are grounded in the evidence.”

The creators of the long-running and enthusiastically insolent TV show “South Park” aren't known to be huge fans of President Donald Trump. However, they’ve decided to adopt one of his ideas — in a way.

They’re changing — at least for the moment — the name of the hugely popular series, which just won the Emmy for outstanding animated program.

In a statement posted on the show’s Instagram page, creators Trey Parker and Matt Stone say they are “changing the name of South Park to SOUTH AMERICA.” The statement comes as Trump, escalating his trade war with Canada, has declared that he's renaming Lake Ontario to be known as “Lake America” in the United States.

It coincides with changes in popular maps

The move by the two satirists, a week before the 29th season premiere of “South Park” — er, “SOUTH AMERICA” — also takes aim at Apple and Google, which have adopted Trump’s changes, as well as the show's own parent company.

Apple has relabeled Lake Ontario to “Lake America” for U.S. users of its Maps app, following cartographic competitor Google.

“Inspired by the bravery and patriotism of Apple and Google, we are changing the name of South Park to SOUTH AMERICA. We especially want to thank our parent company Paramount — a Skydance Capitulation."

The hugely successful “South Park” airs on Paramount-owned Comedy Central. Parker and Stone have taken aim at Paramount’s merger with Skydance. But in July 2025, Paramount announced a five-year renewal deal with Parker and Stone, including streaming rights for previous “South Park” seasons on Paramount+.

During his second term, Trump has also signed an executive order renaming the Gulf of Mexico to the “Gulf of America” even though parts of it lie in international waters. Apple and Google maps also followed suit in that case.

The show's creators have jabbed at Trump before

The decision to rename the show is not the only jab Parker and Stone have recently taken at Trump.

“You finally got your Emmy,” the show posted on Instagram along with a cartoon depiction of the president — with his pants down, surrounded by the show's characters. A recent storyline on the show depicts Trump as romantically involved with Satan.

Canada, too, has not gone unnoticed by the show. In 1999, its foray onto the big screen, “South Park: Bigger, Longer and Uncut,” depicted Canadians as scapegoats of a national parental movement to stop children from swearing — which they blamed on comedians from Canada named “Terrance and Phillip.”

The movie was structured like a Broadway musical, and one of the key “show tunes” it presented was called “Blame Canada.” Its overall point: People can find a way to blame anyone for anything. “It seems that everything's gone wrong since Canada came along,” one character sang.

Other targets of the show's sharp parody over the years have been Saddam Hussein, Tom Cruise, the soft drink Prime and GLP-1 weight-loss drugs.

___

Jocelyn Noveck covers the intersection of media and entertainment for The Associated Press.

News.title: Gay does enough to earn another chance as England dominate again
News.content:
There are two places up for grabs in England’s top three and three players vying: Gay, Jordan Cox and Jacob Bethell, who spent the day on the players’ balcony dropping a reminder of his looming return. A hundred for Durham by Ben McKinney, the one challenger outside of the squad, tweaked the ante up further.

One of Cox or Gay will make way for Bethell when England begin their next series in Johannesburg on December 17, which will be the first Test of the Stephen Fleming era and the first big call he has to make. Cox was on the up after scores of 75 at Headingley and 55 in the first innings at Lord’s, looking the part at No 3. Gay’s luck had run out with a grubber in the second Test and he wasted a couple of 30s in other innings. Cox has opened in first-class cricket and Bethell could also take on the role of Ben Duckett’s partner. The squeeze was on.

But Cox perhaps got a little ahead of himself and played what could be a costly, impetuous shot at Mohammad Abbas to fall for six and hand Gay a chance. Neither Cox nor Gay have been tested on the back foot by genuine pace which will happen at the Wanderers in December but their performances have to be judged against the backdrop of a seam bowlers’ summer. Gay is averaging 27.1 from 10 innings, a number probably worth another 10 runs given the conditions.

His dismissal 20 minutes before the close, playing on driving away from his body, was the one time his footwork was non-existent and Razaullah deserved the breakthrough for coming back and hitting 90mph after tea following so little first-class cricket and a rushed call-up amidst the bloodletting.

News.title: Apple launches its first foldable iPhone – plus other key reveals from the launch
News.content:
The iPhone 18 Pro is more of the same (but pricier than ever)

Unlike previous Apple launches, the standard iPhone 18 model is due to be revealed at a later date. Reports indicate that it will release early next year.

The Wednesday showcase instead focused on the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max models. Aside from the price, the only difference between the two versions is size: the Pro has a 6.3-inch screen, while the Pro Max has a 6.9-inch display.

Both phones have a smaller and less intrusive “Dynamic Island” selfie camera cutout at the top of the screen compared to older models. And like the iPhone Duo, they are powered by Apple’s latest A20 Pro chip, which should be up to 40 per cent faster than the previous iPhone 17 Pro.

The biggest change is with the camera system. The main camera now features a “variable aperture”, which allows you to manually adjust the amount of light passing through the lens, much like a regular camera. This means you should get better nighttime images with extra detail and more control.

Apple says that the 18 Pro Max has the longest-lasting battery life of any iPhone to date, thanks to a new internal heat management system, revamped battery design and efficiencies with the new A20 Pro chip. Battery life is quoted at 36 hours for the 18 Pro when playing video, and 45 hours for the 18 Pro Max. It also charges faster, providing 50 per cent charge after just 15 minutes plugged in.

Elsewhere, the colour-matched aluminium and back glass comes in two new colour choices: burgundy and blue, alongside black and silver.

Both the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are more expensive than last year’s models. The 18 Pro costs £1,199 (a £100 increase), while the 18 Pro Max starts at £1,299. Rival smartphone firm Samsung raised the price of its Galaxy S26 Ultra by £30 earlier this year.

This change aligns with Apple recently raising prices of the iPad and MacBook by up to £300. At the time, CEO Tim Cook said that the price increases were due to the soaring costs of memory chips, which are in high demand thanks to the AI data centre boom.

News.title: Robots with moves and a very light laptop – the best gadgets at Europe’s biggest electronics show
News.content:
Taking place every September in Berlin, the IFA tech and home show stands for “Innovation for All”. It has been held since 1924, and Albert Einstein once attended. The show usually runs for one week and is also open to the public.

Most technology and home appliance brands show off their latest gadgets, whether that’s a never-to-be-sold humanoid robot or their latest coffee machine for your kitchen.

Each year, team Recommended jumps on a plane to see which products we should review and the trends you need to know about. Here is the best of what we saw:

News.title: Man City survive tunnel clash and Porto fury thanks to Haaland double
News.content:
Enzo Maresca takes charge of his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City as they have travelled to Portugal to take on Porto at the Estadio do Dragao. These sides last met during the Champions League group stages during the 2020/21 season. Manchester City won 3-1 at home before the two sides drew 0-0 in this stadium.

Manchester City were busy late on in the transfer window, bringing in both Iliman Ndiaye and Enzo Fernandez as they spent nearly £200m on deadline day alone. They come into tonight’s game off the back of three straight Premier League victories to kick off the Maresca era. Maresca has limited Champions League experience as a manager, which came with Chelsea last season. Manchester City have won their opening game of a Champions League campaign in six of the last seven seasons but this will be the first time since 2015/16 that Manchester City embark on a Champions League campaign without Pep Guardiola at the helm.

“It is a hard place to come [Porto],” said Maresca. “They have started really well. In the last 14/15 games in Europe they lost just one, that shows a difficult place to come, but we will try our best and try to win the game. It is a very, very good team. They have different players, but in terms of the team it is very clear in the way they play. They are aggressive without the ball and on the ball, they have a clear style. But we will try our best and try to win the game. The ambition is the same; try to be ourselves and to win games and then we will see.”

Porto, managed by Francesco Farioli, have won every league game so far this season and already sit four points clear at the summit of Liga Portugal. Farioli takes charge of his first game as a manger in the Champions League and the club make their return to the elite European competition after two seasons away.

“We are going to face one of the big favourites to win the competition,” Farioli said. “It will be a game that will demand that we be at our best, and we know that whenever we step onto the Dragão pitch, something special can happen. I am happy to be in the Champions League for the first time at 37 years old. This will be my first game, but we approach every game with the same attention to detail and the same focus. It is easy for the players to be motivated tomorrow [tonight]. But the key will be our strategy and our ability to execute it, individually and collectively.”

Porto were in the Europa League last season, making it to the quarter-finals, where they were knocked out by Nottingham Forest 2-1 on aggregate. The omens would not appear to be on Porto’s side tonight; they have only won two of their last 16 games against English opposition in major European competition.

News.title: Newcastle scrape past Millwall to extend Jaissle’s unbeaten start
News.content:
Joe Willock’s deft finish ensured Newcastle United survived a tough test against Millwall to keep their excellent run in the Carabao Cup intact.

This competition had been fruitful for Newcastle under former manager Eddie Howe and although this match was hard work – as well as hard to watch at times – his successor Matthias Jaissle guided them through a difficult trip to south-east London.

He called it “job done,” and that was pretty much all it was. “We needed patience on one hand, but also to be passionate and tough. We had the chance [to score] and took it,” he said.

Newcastle have reached the semi-finals of this competition three times in the last four years, but struggled to get any sort of tempo going against their Championship opponents.

You could argue the winning goal came against the run of play late in the second half, moments after Millwall substitute Taïryk Arconte had smashed a low shot against the post.

News.title: Villa end goal drought to finally give Emery’s new era lift-off
News.content:
Unai Emery is building Aston Villa 2.0 and this was a night when his new kids on the block produced clear signs of lift-off for the next chapter.

Emery always springs into life on European nights and his reconstructed team secured their first win and goals of the season to leave Villa’s 1,700 fans singing in the rain.

Ten summer signings have arrived during a summer of upheaval, which included plenty of high-profile departures after the club’s Europa League triumph in May.

Yet this was an evening that will have further energised Emery on his return to the Champions League.

Nicolas Jackson, Zion Suzuki and João Gomes embody this new Villa team and all stood out here in Bruges.

Record £65m signing Jackson’s fine individual goal proved to be the winner to settle a chaotic, absorbing contest with the Belgian Pro League champions.

News.title: Bird flu threatens French foie gras amid new duck cull
News.content:
The latest cull - like previous ones - was undertaken to protect both animal and human health.

Ducks are killed to stop the spread of the disease between farms, as well as to protect the health of farmers and minimise the risk of the virus mutating.

It is thought foie gras itself does not pose a risk to human health, even if it came from a bird-flu-infected duck, because it is almost always heat-treated before it is sold, which effectively destroys the virus, according to Public Health France.

“The consumption of meat, foie gras and eggs – and more generally of any food product based on poultry – presents no risk to humans,” said a spokesman for the Maine-et-Loire prefecture.

Veterinary experts say ducks are especially problematic regarding H5N1 because they can carry the virus without showing symptoms and have been described as the Chevaux de Troie or “Trojan horses” of bird flu.

It is unclear how the birds in the latest outbreak, located on a farm in Longué-Jumelles, contracted the virus, although it is typically spread by wild birds which shed the virus through their droppings.

It is for this reason that British poultry were forced into lockdown or “flockdown” from late October to April of this year.

This included so-called “free-range” birds, which, as the Telegraph reported in November continued to be described as free-range despite never seeing the light of day under a dispensation given by the Department for Environment, Food, and Rural Affairs (DEFRA).

Ducks reared for foie gras typically spend the first 90 days of their lives being reared in their tens of thousands in barns with very little access to natural light.

Animal rights campaigners say most never see water.

They then are put through a rigorous 12-16 day “fattening up” period where they are force-fed through a tube to significantly enlarge their livers, before being slaughtered.

While France introduced a vaccination programme to protect its duck population from bird flu in 2023, the jabs do not entirely stop the virus from getting into a flock.

Data collected by the French Agency for Food, Environmental and Occupational Health & Safety suggested that between 50 and 55 per cent of the country’s ducks are unvaccinated at any given time, due to a 20-day gap between the first and second dose of the vaccine and waning immunity over time.

The ducks subject to the latest bird-flu cull in Western France had received their first dose of the H5N1 vaccine, but not the second, meaning they were not fully protected, according to the disease monitoring firm Airfinity.

The threat to France’s £2 billion foie gras industry comes amid increasing global competition.

Once the dominant producer, it is now being challenged by China, which has rapidly scaled up its output of the delicacy and now accounts for 45 per cent of global production.

A tin of Chinese foie gras costs roughly £3.70, while a typical tin of French foie gras made from duck liver costs between £10 and £15. French foie gras produced from Geese costs anywhere between £70 and £150.

China is also said to operate a more rigorous poultry vaccination programme, according to an analysis by DEFRA.

It applies to all farmed birds in the country, which has managed to keep outbreaks of bird flu on farms relatively low compared with European levels.

The H5N1 avian flu pandemic has now been running for six years and has decimated flocks of farmed chickens and turkeys across the globe.

In the UK alone, more than five million farmed birds have been culled since 2021, costing an estimated £48 million in farmers’ compensation alone.

Last week, the virus was detected on a mink farm in the US state of Utah.

Minks in captivity have previously been described as pandemic “time bombs”. The size and density of fur farms – where thousands of the animals are crammed together in tight proximity – give invading viruses a perfect environment in which to mutate.

The virus has also done huge damage to wild birds and other animals. In South America alone, more than 600,000 wild seabirds have died since 2022.

Dozens of other mammals have been infected and died across the globe, including foxes, otters, sea lions, bears, and seals.

In June, the virus was found in Australia for the first time – the last continent on earth to record a case – and the government has since launched a vaccination programme to protect the country’s rare species, including birds like orange-bellied parrots and black cockatoos.

Scientists have long warned that if H5N1 gains the mutations necessary to spread between people, it could trigger a human-pandemic, something that would be of “enormous concern”, according to the World Health Organization (WHO), given the virus’s 50 per cent case fatality rate.

Sports.title: Man City star told Ryan Giggs 'to leave him alone' after Man Utd transfer probe
Sports.content:
Man City star told Ryan Giggs 'to leave him alone' after Man Utd transfer probe

Ryan Giggs has said he tried to persuade Elliot Anderson to sign for Manchester United this summer after a chance meeting on the golf course in Portugal

View 2 Images Ryan Giggs says he tried to convince Elliot Anderson to sign for Manchester United this summer. (Image: Rio Ferdinand Presents)

Manchester United legend Ryan Giggs says he 'peppered' Elliot Anderson to try and get him to move to Old Trafford this summer following a chance encounter on the golf course while on holiday. The England international was reportedly on Michael Carrick's radar during the summer window, but it was Manchester City who ultimately secured his signature.

‌



Giggs claims Anderson told him 'to leave him alone' after the pair bumped into each other in Portugal in the days before the World Cup. City would go on to splash out £116million on the 23-year-old from Nottingham Forest, while United opted to bring in Youri Tielemans, Carlos Baleba and Andrey Santos to strengthen their midfield options.

‌



Speaking on Rio Ferdinand Presents: The Debrief, Giggs said: "It was literally a few days before he went to the World Cup. I peppered him.

‌



"He didn't know how to take it at first, and then he relaxed a little bit. But for the first four or five holes, we were literally crossing.

Man Utd vs Sabah injury news as six players could miss Champions League opener READ MORE :

Ryan Giggs shares some home truths in brutally honest advice for Marcus Rashford READ MORE :

"And at the end of it, he went, 'will you just let me, leave me alone. Will you just let me play my golf, please? You're in trouble.'"

Ferdinand added: "That's what I do when I see some players. I don't care. You've got to try all sorts to get these deals over.

‌



"It's mad, though. Obviously, the price tag was crazy. And it's just like astronomical money. And Man United ain't got the budget to pay for that."

United would however, splash out a reported £155m on the aforementioned midfield trio in a bid to strengthen Michael Carrick's squad ahead of the summer transfer deadline.

View 2 Images Elliot Anderson (Image: Molly Darlington)

‌



"I think we've brought some really good players into the football club, and improved the squad in different ways, individually but collectively," Carrick told Sky Sports when questioned about United's summer transfer activity.

"I think we've grown. You go into the window and when you come out of it, you want to be stronger than you were at the start. I'm convinced we are that.

"Transfer windows are never straightforward and this window in particular has been challenging for different reasons. There's a lot of money being spent in and around the league itself, and I think we've made the most of the situation that we've found ourselves in.

‌



"That's the world we live in. Teams at certain points are going to spend a lot of money. Sometimes it's going to be more than what we spend, sometimes maybe not.

"We've got to make the most of what we can and understand where we're at. I think we're a very good team, we want to keep getting better."

Sports.title: Declan Rice reaches Premier League title agreement with young Arsenal fan
Sports.content:
Declan Rice reaches Premier League title agreement with young Arsenal fan

Arsenal midfielder Declan Rice has promised to dye his hair with red highlights if the Gunners successfully defend their Premier League title this season

View Image Arsenal midfielder Declan Rice (Image: Getty Images)

Declan Rice has promised to dye his hair with red highlights if Arsenal win the Premier League title again. The Gunners romped to their first top flight in 22 years last season with Rice featuring in all-but two of their league fixtures as Mikel Arteta's side finished seven points ahead of runners-up Manchester United.

‌



Arsenal are the bookmakers' favourites to win the title this season and have enjoyed a perfect start, earning three straight wins and conceding just one goal in the process. They kicked off their campaign with a 3-0 triumph over Coventry City and have subsequently followed that up by beating Aston Villa 1-0 and Chelsea 2-1.

‌



It's a start that leaves them in second in the Premier League table, the same as City, though Enzo Maresca's side occupy top spot having scored one more goal. Hull City, meanwhile, have been the surprise package and sit third on seven points, with Chelsea are in fourth on six points and Brentford rounding out the top five on five points.

‌

Earlier this week, England midfielder Rice was questioned by a young Arsenal supporter about whether he would dye his hair should the Gunners claim the Premier League crown again. When Rice pushed back to ask what colour they had in mind, the fan enthusiastically replied: "Red and white."

Rice then decided to propose a compromise to the supporter, stating he would be willing to have "red highlights in" should Arsenal win the title for the second successive season.

After the fan accepted the arrangement, Rice concluded: "Yes. Buzzing."

Sports.title: Man Utd vs Sabah injury news as six players could miss Champions League opener
Sports.content:
Man Utd vs Sabah injury news as six players could miss Champions League opener

Manchester United will be looking to get their Champions League campaign off to a winning start when they host Azerbaijani side Sabah at Old Trafford on Thursday night

View 2 Images Michael Carrick, manager of Manchester United (Image: Alex Livesey/Getty Images)

Manchester United are preparing to face Sabah in the Champions League, with both teams expected to have some players unavailable for selection. The Red Devils will host the Azerbaijan-based club at Old Trafford on Thursday evening as their league phase campaign officially gets underway.

‌



Michael Carrick has overseen three matches since taking permanent charge of United earlier in the year, and has already been forced to deal with several injuries within his squad.

‌



Unfortunately for United, that will continue on Thursday night when they take on Sabah, with several players expected to miss the fixture.

‌



United go into the game having been forced to settle for a point in a 2-2 draw with Everton over the weekend in the Premier League, a match where several players were on the sidelines through injury.

Rodri rings Valencia player to apologise after chat with Barcelona star gets leaked READ MORE :

Trent Alexander-Arnold and Curtis Jones destroyed by foreign media after Liverpool reunion READ MORE :

Carrick oversaw training at United on Wednesday afternoon, which gave plenty of hints regarding the players the Red Devils boss could call upon for the fixture.

Marcus Rashford was withdrawn with a potential injury concern during the draw with Everton at the weekend, but played a full part in the latest training session. The England international is now expected to be available for United's showdown with Sabah.

‌



There was, however, still no sight of Amad, who continues his recovery from a muscle injury sustained in training before the season got underway.

United were also without Matthijs de Ligt in the session, with the Red Devils confirming the centre-back was taking a rest day. Carrick gave an update on De Ligt's recovery and explained why he remains confident about the defender's return to full fitness.

The United boss told reporters on Wednesday: "We have to see. It's positive. He's trained really well but we're still managing it, when you're out for such a long period of time, you get to the final stages, pushing and pushing, and you've got to manage that last stage.

‌



View 2 Images Luke Shaw of Manchester United (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

"It's important to get that balance right to take the next step. But he's on a good track, in a good place and it's great to have him back around us. Hopefully, some time soon."

‌



Luke Shaw was also absent from the training session, with the club confirming the left-back had been given a rest day alongside De Ligt on Wednesday.

Carrick said: "Yeah, we just gave him an extra recovery day today, Luke. So, obviously, we'll see tomorrow how he is but it's not an ongoing thing or planning like that.

"Off the back of the game the other day, as normal, each individual has different little things we manage and Luke was one of them today."

‌



Whether Shaw will be fit enough to feature against Sabah remains uncertain, while De Ligt — sidelined since November last year with a back problem — will not be rushed back into action. Carlos Baleba and Manuel Ugarte were also missing from the session, with the former continuing his recovery from an ankle problem sustained during pre-season while on duty with Brighton.

Ugarte continues to be a long-term casualty for United as he recuperates from a knee injury sustained while on international duty with Uruguay at the World Cup.

For Sabah, the away side will be without at least one player, with Khayal Aliyev currently ruled out due to a hamstring problem.

Sports.title: Julian Alvarez 'suffering' after failed Arsenal transfer as statement made before Liverpool
Sports.content:
Julian Alvarez 'suffering' after failed Arsenal transfer as statement made before Liverpool

Julian Alvarez is in contention to feature for Atletico Madrid in their Champions League clash against Liverpool on Wednesday, with the Argentine yet to start a game this season

View 2 Images Julian Alvarez is expected to feature for Atletico Madrid against Liverpool (Image: Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images)

Atletico Madrid president Enrique Cerezo has claimed that Julian Alvarez is "suffering" amid a summer of transfer speculation that saw him linked with a move to Barcelona and Arsenal.

‌



Alvarez is yet to start a match for Atletico this season after he came close to leaving the club. The Argentine was understood to be pushing for a move to Barca and made no secret of his desire to quit Atletico.

‌



Arsenal, meanwhile, had placed Alvarez high up on their shortlist as Mikel Arteta tried to strengthen his front line, with sporting director Andrea Berta trying to convince the ex-Manchester City man to move back to the Premier League, having worked with him at Atletico.

‌



Despite Barca offering more than £86million and fierce backlash from the Atletico supporters, Diego Simeone's side ended up keeping hold of Alvarez beyond the transfer deadline. With that, Alvarez is in contention to feature for Atletico ahead of their Champions League opener against Liverpool on Wednesday after being named in the travelling squad.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Speaking hours before the game at Anfield, Cerezo provided an update on Alvarez's current condition and believes he is still coming to terms of failing to secure a move away from Atletico.

In an interview with Spanish newspaper Sport, Cerezo said: "I see Alvarez in good shape, but the truth is that he is suffering after what happened recently, and that is a cause for concern."

He added: "I think his recovery is going well, and when the coach sees that the time is right, he will return to play. The Julian case is closed."

‌



Alvarez, who came off the bench in Saturday's 3-0 defeat at Athletic Club, has been named in Atletico's travelling squad for the Liverpool fixture and is anticipated to feature as a substitute, after Diego Simeone admitted he doesn't see the ex-Manchester City man "starting yet".

When asked about Alvarez in his pre-Liverpool press conference, Simeone said: "Julian is still developing; I don't see him starting yet, but he'll help us as the game progresses."

View 2 Images Julian Alvarez is now back in the fold at Atletico Madrid (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Regarding Atletico's other striking options, both Jonathan David and Alexander Sorloth are doubts, suggesting Lee Kang-in and Alex Baena could once again be deployed up front.

"Jonathan arrived very recently and couldn't play the other day [against Athletic Club] due to a problem," Simeone said. "[Sorloth's] recovering. He has this injury that's keeping him from playing. We need him; he's important, whether it's for 90, 60 or 20 minutes. He gives us things we don't have in the team right now. Hopefully, he'll be back soon."

Simeone added: "It's very important for the club that the final is at the Metropolitano. For us, we have to work incredibly hard to be able to aspire to that privileged position.

‌



"We're in a growth phase, settling in; there are many new players, the situation with Julian, David's arrival at the end of the transfer window, the national team players who arrived late and nobody cares about them anymore. Little by little, we'll find our rhythm."

Alvarez has managed just 55 minutes of football all season, but looks set to build on that and clock up further game time against Liverpool.

Sports.title: Erling Haaland accuses Porto star of 'grabbing bottom' after angry bust-up on pitch
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland accuses Porto star of 'grabbing bottom' after angry bust-up on pitch

Erling Haaland was the Manchester City hero again in their Champions League victory over FC Porto, with the Norwegian striker notching both goals at the Estadio do Dragao

View 2 Images Erling Haaland clashes with Pablo Rosario (Image: Clive Brunskill)

Erling Haaland has claimed Pablo Rosario 'grabbed his bottom' as the two wrestled during Manchester City's fiery clash with Porto in the Champions League.

‌



Haaland scored twice in Portugal to give City a victory in their opening fixture, which was bad-tempered throughout. The Norway international and Rosario were both cautioned for a clash on the pitch, while there was also a confrontation between players and staff in the tunnel at half-time.

‌



Opening up on his tussle with Rosario, Haaland claimed the defender ended up grabbing his bottom during an interview with Norwegian television.

‌



“I was really keen on a hat-trick and it seemed like he [Rosario] was very eager to stop me from getting it. It was a little interesting, that. You’ll be seeing a picture where he’s grabbing my bottom... it’ll be interesting to see that picture,” he said.

Haaland, whose brace means he is now City's joint all-time top scorer in the Champions League with Sergio Aguero on 36 goals, admitted that Rosario and his Porto team-mates gave Enzo Maresca's side a real game.

‌



The Porto goalkeeper, Diogo Costa, had kept the Portuguese giants in the game with a string of fine saves in the first half before Haaland stuck. The 26-year-old broke the deadlock just two minutes after the restart before killing off any chance of the hosts snatching a share of the spoils with a 91st minute clincher.

“It was a difficult fight, man against man. They are a top team. Honestly, they are impressive,” he told Amazon Prime post-match.

View 2 Images Haaland scored both goals in Manchester City's 2-0 win over FC Porto (Image: Clive Brunskill/Getty Images)

‌



“I think honestly we controlled the first half. A bit uncomfortable when they came a bit high, but we created a lot of chances. I could easily have had a lot more goals, but second half we scored, and they pushed us for a good 25 minutes, but again we managed to hold through and then finish the game.

“I think these are the games that we have to win, and we have had a great start to the season. In the Champions League you have to win games because, if not, you suddenly get all the pressure, and then you never know what's going to happen.”

Sports.title: Michael Carrick explains why Luke Shaw missed Man Utd training with transfer failure clear
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick explains why Luke Shaw missed Man Utd training with transfer failure clear

Manchester United host Sabah in their opening Champions League game of the season on Thursday night and Michael Carrick has been forced to address concerns over Luke Shaw

View 2 Images Michael Carrick spoke ahead of Manchester United's first Champions League tie (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United's decision not to sign a left-back in the summer transfer window has been put under scrutiny after Luke Shaw missed a training session ahead of their opening Champions League game of the season.

‌



United went into the transfer window keen to bring in some competition for Shaw, but failed to sign one, with top target Lewis Hall unavailable from Newcastle. Shaw played all 38 Premier League games for United last season, but the club have a tougher challenge this season having returned to the Champions League.

‌



The challenge facing Michael Carrick is clear this week, with the derby against Manchester City coming on Sunday on the back of Thursday's Champions League game against debutants Sabah. With just one senior specialist left-back in the squad, Shaw's fitness and durability will come under the microscope.

‌



The 31-year-old was absent from Wednesday's training session, raising concerns over his availability. But Carrick played down any hint of an injury in his pre-match press conference.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"We just gave him an extra recovery day today," he said. "We'll see by tomorrow how he is, but it's not an ongoing thing or a plan or anything like that. It was just off the back of the game the other day. Each individual has kind of different little things that we manage and Luke was one of them today."

With academy graduate left-back Harry Amass not in the squad, it was Noussair Mazraoui who replaced Shaw off the bench in the 2-2 draw with Everton on the weekend. Mazraoui, Patrick Dorgu and Diogo Dalot are the most likely alternatives to Shaw.

Carrick knows he will have to use his squad to manage the busy fixture schedule. Asked whether rotation would come against the team from Azerbaijan on Thursday night at Old Trafford, Carrick made his approach clear.

‌



View 2 Images Luke Shaw is the only senior specialist left-back at Manchester United (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

"It's a balanced view, that's why we've got the squad," he said. "We need to adapt to certain strengths and different ways of playing. We play Thursday, Wednesday, it's about managing the group and trusting them and anyone who can play will play."

The Manchester Derby comes quickly on the back of Thursday's game, but Carrick refused to complain. "I'm not concerned," he said. "It's not ideal, but it's not something we can do much about. We've got to deal with the cards we were dealt."

‌



The depth in defence has been given a boost by the return to training of Matthias de Ligt, who hasn't played since the end of November, having undergone back surgery in May.

"It's positive. Matta has trained really well," said Carrick. "I think when you're out for such a long period of time and you get right to the final stages and you push and you push, you've got to manage that last stage. It's important.

"We've got to get that balance right for when to take the next step. But he's on a good track, he's in a good place, and it's great to have him back around us, and hopefully it'll be sometime soon."

Sports.title: Man City and Premier League 'braced for £100m bill' as huge claim made about 115 charges case
Sports.content:
Man City and Premier League 'braced for £100m bill' as huge claim made about 115 charges case

The Premier League's legal battle with Manchester City has still not seen a result and has been ongoing for almost two years since the 12-week hearing finished in 2024

View 2 Images The outcome of the Premier League's legal battle with Manchester City is still unknown (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

Manchester City and the Premier League's legal battle is estimated to have cost each over £100m and may have already reached the appeal stage, according to football finance expert Kieran Maguire. City were charged with 115 breaches of the Premier League's financial rules in February 2023, but no result has been forthcoming.

‌



Maguire, who admits he has no evidence to support such a suspicion, said he would not be surprised if one party were appealing an initial finding, given the silence around the case. He highlighted a similar situation with Chelsea, where the news did not emerge until after their appeal over 78 charges.

‌



A 12-week hearing into the charges against City concluded in December 2024. With the two-year mark approaching, the independent commission is yet to publish a ruling on the complex case, with City strongly denying the allegations they face.

‌



"We are probably talking hundreds and hundreds of thousands of pieces of evidence, and they have to be gone through with a fine-tooth comb," Maguire said on the Rest is Football podcast.

"We saw with the Chelsea case, where Chelsea had 78 charges, that the verdict was given and Chelsea effectively appealed and that took another 3 or 4 months to work out.

‌



"So we could be in a situation, and I have no evidence to back this up, that there has been a decision made on Manchester City and either the Premier League or Manchester City have immediately appealed and we are now actually working out way through the appeal process to get a final, final answer. We didn't know that (there was an appeal) in terms of Chelsea."

Mirror Sport have approached Manchester City and the Premier League for comment.

In May, it was suggested that a result could still be two years away. The scale of the charges and the severity of the accusations have ensured a long wait for an unprecedented case in English football.

‌



Among City's charges are 54 allegations of failing to provide accurate and up-to-date financial information from 2009 until 2018. They also face 14 alleged breaches of failing to provide accurate financial reports of player and manager compensation over the same period.

View 2 Images Manchester City were handed 115 charges over three years ago. (Image: Molly Darlington/Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



"We are now almost two years since the commission first sat, it commenced in September 2024," Maguire said. "It took around about 10-12 weeks to hear all the evidence. As one lawyer said to me, if there are 115 charges, there are 115 defences, so it makes it difficult.

"You have got three people sitting on the commission, all of whom are very high-powered people in their own right, so getting them into the same room at the same time over the course of the last 18-20 months has proven to be very difficult.

"Then, from what I understand and there has been very much a news blackout, you have got to give the people and professionals involved a lot of credit. There are no leaks, no WhatsApp groups with gossip."

‌

The wait is proving costly for both the Premier League and City, however. Maguire believes both will have racked up nine-figure bills.

"These charges are so serious that it is difficult to see how the board of Manchester City could survive if they lose the case and it would be hugely embarrassing for the Premier League if they lose the case because the legal costs for both parties are probably in excess of £100m," Maguire added.

‌



Premier League chief Richard Masters has admitted that the process has taken longer than he hoped. Speaking last month he suggested he was unable to provide an update and that the system must be allowed to take its course.

"Our rules are very clear about that - I have to keep everything confidential until we're ready to hand down a decision and be clear about it," he said. "I can't give any update on timing or what's happening.

"There's only one available route through this, which is to allow the process to take its course. It has taken longer than expected, and I do understand the frustrations."

Article continues below

"I've already said the commission need the time and the space to do their job," he added. "In the end, the Premier League's role is to put allegations, if the evidence is strong enough, in front of an independent commission and allow that commission to establish the truth, and that shouldn't be qualified by the amount of time it takes to get there."

Sports.title: Gurney called up to World Series Finals after withdrawals due to visa issues
Sports.content:
Daryl Gurney has been called up to play at the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam after visa issues led to the withdrawal of Philippines players Lourence Ilagan and Alexis Toylo from the September 17-20 event.

Northern Ireland's Gurney and the Netherlands' Maik Kuivenhoven were the highest-ranked players on the reserve list and have replaced Ilagan and Toylo respectively after the pair did not receive a decision on their Schengen visa applications before having to travel to China this week for the final two events of the PDC Asian Tour season.

Gurney will face reigning tournament champion and home favourite Michael van Gerwen in the first round at AFAS Live on Thursday September 17, while Kuivenhoven plays Jonny Clayton the following day.

Luke Littler, the 2024 champion who was beaten 11-7 by Van Gerwen in last year's final, heads to Amsterdam aiming to keep his bid for the first-ever clean sweep of majors in one year on track.

The world champion plays Danny Noppert in round one.

Sports.title: Tongue tears through sorry Pakistan as England earn lead on day one
Sports.content:
England dominated a sorry-looking Pakistan yet again on day one of the third Test at Edgbaston, bowling the tourists out for 133 before closing on 156-4, with a 23-run lead.

Emilio Gay (60) and Harry Brook (52no) each struck fifties in the final session to rescue England from 39-3 after their own top-order wobble, in which Joe Root (8) was pinned lbw for a 10th time in 13 innings by Pakistan's hugely-impressive debutant pacer Razaullah (2-42).

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player 21-year-old Razaullah gets the wicket of Joe Root on his Test debut.

Root had earlier opted to insert the visitors at the toss in overcast conditions, but it wasn't long before his side were preparing to bat anyway, as Pakistan lasted just 33.5 overs - their shortest innings in a series full of disappointing batting displays.

Score summary - England vs Pakistan, third Test, Edgbaston Pakistan 133 all out in 33.5 overs in first innings (put in to bat): Saud Shakeel (43), Mohammad Abbas (21); Josh Tongue (4-42), Ollie Robinson (3-15), Jofra Archer (3-25) England 156-4 after 39 overs in first innings (lead by 23 runs): Emilio Gay (60), Harry Brook (52no); Razaullah (2-42)

Seven wickets fell in a chaotic morning session which saw Ollie Robinson (3-15) claim his 100th in Test cricket, before the innings was wrapped up soon after lunch.

Josh Tongue finished with 4-42, dismantling the stumps of Pakistan captain Babar Azam (7), Mohammad Imran (5) and lone bright spark Saud Shakeel (43), while Jofra Archer proved potent once more, taking 3-25.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Josh Tongue led England's wickets on day one of the third Test with Pakistan, ending on 4-42.

The tourists failed to bat out a full 90 overs - the equivalent of a day's play - across their two innings in either of the first two Tests, and they will struggle to buck that trend barring a stunning turnaround this week.

Pakistan's squad overhaul feeds into chaotic first innings

Pakistan's 194-run defeat at Lord's, which saw them lose the series with a match to spare, prompted an unprecedented overhaul of their squad and coaching staff prior to the series finale in Birmingham.

Seven players were dropped from the squad altogether, with four changes made to their starting XI and three of the newcomers making their Test debut.

The only one with prior experience was opener Saim Ayub who, while no doubt grateful for the call-up, must have been wondering what he'd got himself into when trapped for a 10-ball duck by Robinson in only the third over.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ollie Robinson gets England's first wicket in their third Test against Pakistan, dismissing Saim Ayub.

Robinson also removed Abdullah Shafique (3) caught in the gully, the wicket sandwiched between a couple of freebies for Archer handed out by scrambled Pakistan batters - Azan Awais (9) and Shan Masood (5) both spooning simple catches to midwicket, the latter's particularly galling, as the visitors slipped to 26-4.

Tongue then produced the prototypical fast bowler's delivery, angling in, nipping away and knocking back the top of off stump to see off Babar, while he added debutants Ghazi Ghori (4), lbw, and Imran, to a devastating yorker, prior to lunch.

Razaullah (11), much like he would do later with his bowling, caught the eye with a couple of hefty swings of the willow either side of lunch before nicking Robinson to Ben Duckett, who made amends for a couple of earlier drops in the slips - Azan, three dliveries prior to his dismissal, and Saud when on seven.

Saud was next to be castled by Tongue, before Mohammad Abbas (21) and Mohammad Ali (5no) hung around and showed a great deal more fight than some of their top-order team-mates to add 26 for the final wicket - the highest partnership of a miserable innings.

Ali had taken a painful blow on the ankle when batting, but was fit enough to open the bowling and claimed the early wicket of Duckett (11), flashing an edged to second slip in the fourth over.

Jordan Cox (4) wasted a review on a plumb lbw decision against Abbas, before Root departed to Razaullah's fourth delivery in Test cricket, a devastating nip-backer from the 21-year-old talent.

Gay and Brook rebuilt impressively, sharing in a 104-run partnership for the fourth wicket that pushed England into the lead before Razaullah returned to bowling the former off an inside edge.

Tongue chuffed with wobble-seam success on first day

England fast bowler Josh Tongue, speaking to Sky Sports Cricket:

Image: England's Josh Tongue celebrates one of his four wickets on day one against Pakistan at Edgbaston

"Really pleased with the day. Coming here this morning, winning the toss, putting Pakistan in to bat, then bowling them out for 130-odd, we're in a really strong position.

"Even a couple of days out it looked a good pitch, so to bowl them out cheaply on a decent-looking pitch, I thought we bowled really well.

"There's probably a tiny bit of pressure on us to make sure we put the balls in the right areas, but how we started today, with Archer and Robinson getting them four down... it meant that when I came on, I thought I could be aggressive with that line and length.

"I've been working on a wobble in the nets this week, and that came out nice. I spoke to Robbo quite a bit about it; it's just trial and error.

"I tried it, and it got me a wicket!

"I thought as a collective we've been very good the whole series, and we showed that again today."

'X-factor Razaullah the bright spark Pakistan needed'

Sky Sports Cricket's Nasser Hussain:

"Pakistan have been calling out for something different from their bowlers for a long while.

"It is nice to watch that spell from Razaullah that had something, that had a point of difference, had some pace.

Image: Pakistan fast bowler Razaullah celebrates the wicket of England opener Emilio Gay on the first evening of the third Test at Edgbaston

"It hurried one of the greatest batters there has ever been in Joe Root, and got him out."

Sky Sports Cricket's Urooj Mumtaz:

"Twenty-one-years-old, first time on a plane out of Pakistan, onto a cricketing tour and he gets one of the greatest of all time with his fourth delivery!

"89mph and then just ramped it up to 91mph. And the best part was that the pace throughout his spells did not drop.

"An inspired selection. They just needed that X-factor.

"The conveyor belt is not broken, it is the system."

Sports.title: Doyle: Waardah the one to beat in the Park Hill
Sports.content:
Our ambassador Hollie Doyle gives her verdict on the action from Town Moor, providing her take on the Park Hill, May Hill and Sales Race.

Burrows holds key to 'fillies' Leger'

The race they call the Fillies' Leger, the Betfred Park Hill Fillies' Stakes (3.00), is one of the highlights of the opening day of the Betfred St Leger Festival at Doncaster on Thursday and I expect a competitive renewal to go the way of the Owen Burrows-trained Waardah.

She has run two big races in a light campaign in pattern company this year, including in the Group Two Lillie Langtry Stakes at the Qatar Goodwood Festival, only to pay the price for a touch of freshness early in the race - her first since May.

With a hood fitted for the first time, she can prove too good for some classy types including Fairy Glen who shone out in Meydan in the spring when taking the Dubai Gold Cup over two miles from Friday's probable Doncaster Cup favourite Caballo De Mar.

Image: Waardah, ridden by jockey Callum Rodriguez, on their way to winning the Lillie Langtry at Glorious Goodwood

Simon and Ed Crisford's mare has proven form on the back of a break so shouldn't be troubled by a four-month absence and her stamina beyond this extended mile-and-three-quarter trip is assured.

Irish filly looks strong in May Hill

Godolphin's filly Musical Times brings a burgeoning reputation to the other Group Two on the opening day at Doncaster, the Betfred May Hill Stakes (3.35) for the two-year-olds.

Unbeaten in novice races at Newmarket and Yarmouth and on course for a possible crack at the Group One Fillies' Mile, this exciting daughter of Lope De Vega is a fascinating runner in this recognised Classic trial.

However, she hasn't beaten a lot at this stage so I'm taking her on with Irish raider Sea Of Rain, who has already proven herself at a high level with victory in a Group Three at the Curragh last time. Jim Bolger's filly has plenty of experience and won't mind a bit of cut in the ground.

Can't see past Vegas in valuable sales race

I just can't see past the likely favourite Night In Vegas in the big juvenile cavalry charge on the opening day, the Weatherbys £300,000 2-Y-O Stakes (1.50).

Eve Johnson Houghton's colt boasts a lofty rating of 102 yet gets a considerable amount of weight from many of his closest rivals under the terms of this race. His credentials are impeccable with a valuable auction race success at Newmarket last time coming on the back of a creditable third in the Group Two Richmond Stakes at the Goodwood Festival.

I'm hoping to see my husband Tom (Marquand) go well on William Haggas's God Given Talent who was unlucky in running when fourth in a hot nursery at York's Ebor Festival on his first start for the yards since leaving James Ferguson.

Satellite Of Love, who like God Given Talent has a rating of 91, can also play a part. Clive Cox's colt was unbeaten in his first two starts before finishing a well beaten fifth behind the thrown-in Group One winner Sun Goddess in that York sales race.

Cox filly can make winning nursery debut

Art Of Life is yet to get her head in front but can make a winning debut out of novice company in the British Stallion Studs 'Carrie Red' EBF Fillies' Nursery Handicap (1.15) on Thursday.

Cox's filly has been unlucky to bump into a couple of promising types at Newbury, including when a shade too keen behind Tom's hot favourite Sweetwonderfulyou last time.

I marginally prefer her to Richard Spencer's likely favourite Speed Of Sound, a lovely Sioux Nation filly who ran a stormer at the weights behind Sun Goddess in that valuable sales race at York.

At a much bigger price, Richard Hannon's Rollthedicebaby has the talent to get back on track off an easing mark after finishing in the pack behind Speed Of Sound on the Knavesmire.

King can reign back in handicap grade

Tom and his boss William have the one they all have to beat in the mile and a quarter Pertemps Network Handicap (2.25) on the opening day.

King Of Earth impressed me when taking a valuable Curragh handicap in the summer in first time cheekpieces and can be forgiven his effort last time in Group Three company at York.

Back in a handicap with the ground and a good draw in his favour, he can get quickly back on track at the possible expense of John and Thady Gosden's Runman.

It's early days for the son of Frankel who put a two-month break behind him to win over this trip at Newbury last time. He looks very well treated off just a three-pound higher mark and will enjoy conditions on Town Moor.

Hollie Doyle was speaking to Sky Sports Racing's Simon Mapletoft.

Watch every race of the Betfred St Leger Festival live on Sky Sports Racing (Sky 415 | Virgin 512) from Thursday 10th to Sunday 13th September.

Sports.title: Napoli v Arsenal: Champions League – live
Sports.content:
4m ago 15.57 EDT Half-time fag break postbag ... which for some reason is tobacco-infused. “Well, sir, can they boogie without the Great Scott? Presumably Mr McT is in the stand somewhere, a crafty fag on the go, cupped between thumb and index finger and held behind the back, just in case the cameras spot him” – Justin Kavanagh “Just checking: Gyökeres is still there, right? He hasn’t gone for a lie down or some mid-half snus?” – Adam Walker “I understand that winning games builds psychological momentum, but I feel that Arteta could use some of these essentially meaningless league phase matches to give his most overworked players the night off. Does Rice need to be on the field? Yeah, if you want to maximise your chances of winning this game. But given how exhausted he looked at the end of last season, it might be good to rest him” – Kári Tulinius “Can you put that photo of Kai Havertz back up? At least then Arsenal fans will have a useful striker to look at. And it’d be no more immoble than the one on the pitch” – Charles Anaki [Click here to relive some of that Hot Havertz Action] The Joy of Six: smoking sports stars Read more Share

11m ago 15.49 EDT HALF TIME: Napoli 0-0 Arsenal It’s been good, but not great. Share

12m ago 15.49 EDT 45 min +2: Saka goes long. There’s a bit of pinball, before Hincapie tries to catch Meret out with a cheeky threaded shot towards the bottom left. There’s no pace on the shot, and it’s easy for the keeper. Share

13m ago 15.48 EDT 45 min +1: The first of two additional minutes, and Konsa’s sheer determination down the right wins Arsenal a corner. Just enough time to take it! Share

13m ago 15.47 EDT 45 min: Arsenal should be leading. Odegaard slides a pass down the inside-right channel to release Saka into the Napoli box. Saka is one on one with Meret, and looks for the top left, but gets it all wrong, the ball sailing miles off target to the left. The offside flag pops up to momentarily save Saka’s blushes … but replays show he was comfortably onside. That’s a huge opportunity passed up. Share

15m ago 15.45 EDT 43 min: The free kick, then. A big faff, and a big waste. But Arsenal come again, Odegaard curling in from the left. Meret, who looks fit and healthy to the naked and untrained eye, punches clear acrobatically. Share

16m ago 15.44 EDT 42 min: This game has slipped into Basketball Mode. Saka with a dribble down the right. His cutback for Rice is intercepted. Olivera probes down the left but can’t get past Konsa. Eze scampers up the other end, and is skittled by Gilmour, who goes into the book. A free kick 30 yards out, just to the left of centre. Share

18m ago 15.43 EDT 40 min: Olivera swats Saka off the ball and sends Santos off on a wild run down the left. Santos nearly gets the better of Konsa … but the Arsenal defender somehow sticks to his side like glue, and eventually does some swatting of his own. Santos goes over, and wants a free kick, but he’s not getting one. Share

20m ago 15.41 EDT 39 min: Politano’s in-swinging shot from the right flies straight at Raya. Arsenal counter, and Saka hoicks a dreadful effort miles over the bar. Share

20m ago 15.40 EDT 38 min: … though having said that, Napoli’s back-up keeper Milinković-Savić is furiously prepping in the dugout. Meret puts his boot through a clearance, meanwhile, so perhaps all’s well. Let’s see. Share

22m ago 15.39 EDT 37 min: Meret is fine to continue, and restarts the game. Everyone refreshed. Share

23m ago 15.38 EDT 36 min: The game doesn’t restart immediately, because Meret has a problem. On come the physio. Everyone else takes the opportunity to snorkel some isotonic treats. Share

24m ago 15.37 EDT 35 min: Rice buys a ticket from 25 yards. High and wide. Share

24m ago 15.36 EDT 34 min: Hojlund chases a pass down the inside-right, holds off Gabriel, and lays off to De Bruyne, whose shot balloons off Gabriel and out for a corner … but Napoli don’t get the set piece, because the flag goes up for offside. It was a close one, though, Hojlund pretty much level with Gabriel at the start of the chase. Had Napoli scored from the move, VAR would have had some work to do. Share

26m ago 15.34 EDT 32 min: Hincapie sends a cross in from a tight spot on the left … and nearly catches Meret out at his near post. Meret does well to claw the ball out and away. Not entirely sure Hincapie meant that, but if he did, it was a super-cheeky gamble and nearly paid out. Share

28m ago 15.32 EDT 30 min: Santos crosses from the left and nearly finds De Bruyne in the middle, six yards out, but Konsa is on point to block and clear. Both teams searching furiously for the opener. Share

29m ago 15.31 EDT 29 min: Eze cuts in from the left and drags a shot wide left. He grimaces and sucks in some air. It was a good chance. Arsenal come again, Saka jinking in from the right before shanking a weak effort wide left. Another good chance spurned. View image in fullscreen Arsenal's Eberechi Eze (right) attempts a shot on goal. Photograph: Agostino Gemito/PA Share Updated at 15.46 EDT

31m ago 15.29 EDT 27 min: Saka plays a ball in from the right to tee up Merino on the edge of the Napoli D. Merino takes a heavy touch, allowing De Bruyne to nip in, steal the ball, and draw a foul. You’ve seen yellows given for less, but if this referee wasn’t going to book Eze earlier, he’s certainly not going to show one for that. Share

34m ago 15.27 EDT 25 min: Time and space for Politano out on the right. But not that much time and space. He faffs around, and when he eventually decides to attempt a cross, he’s closed down by Hincapie. Share

35m ago 15.25 EDT 23 min: … Rice dribbles a weak shot straight at Meret. Napoli break quickly again, and Santos takes aim from a tight angle on the left. It’s blocked easily by White. Share

36m ago 15.24 EDT 22 min: Saka cuts in from the right and crosses long. Eze heads back across the face of goal for Merino, who rams a header goalwards from six yards. But it’s straight at Meret, who tips over. Great save, but the keeper shouldn’t have been given the chance to make one. You’d expect Merino to bury that. And from the corner … View image in fullscreen Napoli's keeper Alex Meret (centre) makes a save from Arsenal's Mikel Merino. Photograph: Gregorio Borgia/AP Share Updated at 15.47 EDT

38m ago 15.22 EDT 20 min: A long ball down the middle nearly releases Hojlund on goal. Gabriel grapples with the striker and does just enough to put him off. Both teams look good going forward. Share

39m ago 15.21 EDT 19 min: De Bruyne spins around Eze’s flailing leg and is brought down. No idea why Eze isn’t booked, but the Arsenal player gets away with it. De Bruyne is fuming. Share

41m ago 15.20 EDT 18 min: Politano finds some space down the right but his looping cross is easy pickings for Raya. Better from Napoli, though; the hosts are working their way into this match after a slow start. Share

42m ago 15.19 EDT 16 min: De Bruyne should release Santos on the left but tries a trickier pass for Hojlund down the middle. It’s no good. The ball breaks to Politano, who shoots harmlessly from his position on the right. Share

43m ago 15.17 EDT 15 min: Napoli spend some time patiently passing around the back. Suddenly Di Lorenzo is released down the right. He rolls infield for De Bruyne, who pearls a shot straight at Raya. It’s too hot to handle. Raya spills, but Santos can’t get to the rebound. White pings it off the Napoli man and it’s a goal kick. Share

46m ago 15.15 EDT 13 min: Eze is clipped out on the left and Odegaard sends the free kick diagonally into the Napoli box. Gabriel doesn’t win the header. Napoli clear. Politano acrobatically keeps the ball in play out on the left, but only manages to set Arsenal off on the attack again. The ball’s sent into the middle, where Saka bicycle kicks straight into Meret’s arms. Arsenal full of confidence. Share

47m ago 15.13 EDT 11 min: Arsenal continue to stroke it around nicely, and after a few triangles down the right are completed, Saka releases Rice into the box with a sliderule pass. Rice’s attempt at a cutback is no good, and hacked clear. Share

49m ago 15.12 EDT 9 min: One corner leads to another, and from the second, Napoli tear clear on the counter. Hojlund bombs up the inside-right channel and feeds Santos on the overlap. Santos enters the box and slices a cross over the bar and out for a goal kick. That was a good opportunity for Napoli. Share

50m ago 15.10 EDT 8 min: It’s all the all-reds of Arsenal in these early exchanges. Eze has a whack from distance and the ball deflects out for the first corner of the match. Rice to take, with Napoli having left four players on the halfway line, Chelsea-at-the-weekend style. Share

51m ago 15.09 EDT 7 min: Some more action for White down the right. He chases what looks like a lost cause and digs out a cross. Easy for Meret, with no Arsenal player anywhere near the keeper. Share

53m ago 15.08 EDT 6 min: Odegaard and White combine neatly down the right and find Saka in a small pocket of space inside the Napoli box. Saka has nanoseconds to shoot, and his effort is easily and effectively blocked. Nice move, though. Share

55m ago 15.06 EDT 4 min: De Bruyne finds a little bit of space out on the right, and curls a low cross into the Arsenal box. There’s no Napoli presence within, and it’s easy for Raya. Share

55m ago 15.05 EDT 2 min: Arsenal are wearing red shorts. Full marks for considering those with colour blindness, and acting with compassion. It doesn’t look good, mind. It’s just not Arsenal. Share
