World.title: 'Jou ma se ****' - Pemmy Majodina loses cool during community engagement
World.content:
KOUGA - Water and Sanitation Minister Pemmy Majodina's meeting with the Kouga community descended into chaos.

Profanities were exchanged between Majodina and a community member during a launch of an upgraded pump station.

This was a dramatic turn of events which left the community in shock.

A community member who was being escorted out of the venue said "jou ma se ****" to Majodina and she responded by saying "Phuma! Jou ma se **** ook."

eNCA spoke to Kyle Minnaar, an administrator in the Kouga Municipality, who detailed the heated meeting with the community.

According to Minnaar, the day started with the launch before moving to government community engagement.

Minnaar said, two serious concerns came out of that meeting, the first being that the meeting was heavily politicised and the second was the chaos which erupted.

“During the Q&A session, a resident who was forced out of the hall was disagreeing with another resident who was talking. I suppose he talked out of turn when the Minister requested that this resident be removed from the hall. Whilst he was walking out of the hall, she passed the insult.”

Minnaar said he was disappointed with the Minister.

He said while he notes that the community member who was escorted out may have been guilty of speaking out of turn, but that is not enough reason for the Minister to respond in that manner.

World.title: Evacuations in Malibu after waves open sinkhole at Nicolas Cage's house
World.content:
MALIBU - People living in an upmarket coastal stretch of Malibu were under an evacuation order Wednesday after a giant sinkhole opened up on the driveway of a beachfront home belonging to Oscar-winning US actor Nicolas Cage.

The enormous hole appeared Tuesday as heavy surf, brought by the after-effects of a hurricane, pounded the exclusive coastline, which is home to some of California's wealthiest people and a host of celebrities.

Photographs of the crater, estimated to be as much as 60 feet (18 meters) wide in places, showed it contained concrete, tiles and a portable toilet that appeared to have been placed at the multi-million dollar home for use by workmen who were doing alterations.

By Tuesday evening, the sinkhole was around 25 feet deep, as waves from the churning Pacific Ocean continued to eat away at the coastline, lapping around the stanchions that support the house which the "Leaving Las Vegas" actor bought for $10.5 million.

Malibu city officials issued an evacuation order affecting dozens of homes in some of the most sought-after real estate in Southern California.

"The Director of Emergency Services of the City of Malibu has declared the existence of a local emergency following a large sinkhole forming near 31630 Sea Level Drive," an announcement said.

"An evacuation order is in effect for all affected properties. Sheriff Deputies have notified residents in person, and a digital alert has been issued by the City."

South of Los Angeles, truckloads of boulders had been placed along a stretch of beach in Dana Point in an effort to protect properties in a spot where seven homes have already been declared uninhabitable, with one partially collapsing into the sea.

Richard Thompson, a meteorologist with the National Weather Service, told AFP on Tuesday that coastal waters were being roiled by the remnants of Hurricane Marie.

"There were some pretty significant surf and swells across area in the last several days," he said.

"At the height of the surf and swell, we had some very significant wave heights of 10 up to 15 feet (3.0-4.5 meters) in some spots, along with significant beach erosion."

This week Hurricane Lowell lashed Hawaii with damaging winds, heavy rainfall and powerful floods, blacking out power across most of one island.

A near-record-strength El Nino climate episode is warming the waters of the Pacific Ocean and promoting the formation of powerful storms.

While the warming phase is a natural phenomenon, scientists believe the human-caused heating of the climate could make its effects much larger.

World.title: Lower electricity prices, jobs creation: Ramaphosa makes promises in Thembisa
World.content:
THEMBISA - ANC President Cyril Ramaphosa said government is working to ease pressure on households, while attracting investment and creating jobs.

Speaking on the campaign trail in Thembisa, he acknowledged that weak economic growth remains a challenge.

Ramaphosa said measures are being put in place to bring down electricity prices and grow the economy.

"That is why we are embarking on restructuring of our electricity sector so that prices can be brought down on an overall basis," Ramaphosa said.

He also noted concerns over unemployment, but Ramaphosa said efforts are being made to attract investment to make sure that the economy grows.

World.title: '800 000 mandrax tablets produced a day': Hawks uncover drug lab in Pretoria
World.content:
PREOTRIA - Hawks have cracked a drug syndicate after pouncing on another drug lab, this time in Erasmia, west of Pretoria.

The lab is said to have allegedly been producing approximately 800 000 mandrax tablets a day.

Added to this, police believe this is also the discovery of a new establishment that purports to be manufacturing crystal meth.

READ | R800,000 cocaine haul lands man in custody at OR Tambo

According to Deputy National Commissioner for Policing Tebello Mosikili, two foreign nationals were arrested during the raid on the clandestine mandrax lab and drugs were seized.

“This is a major blow to a large-scale criminal syndicate and to the illicit drug supply chain in South Africa. Eight hundred thousand tablets a day is not just a small number. “By dismantling this facility, we are disrupting the production capacity of a network capable of flooding our communities with hundreds of thousands of mandrax tablets every single day,” Mosikili said.

According to Mosikili, the operation was intelligence-led, with crime intelligence having monitored activities and movements at this small holding for some time.

She said authorities are now working on establishing the source of the drugs.

World.title: Unless doctor says otherwise, Mapisa-Nqakula trial unlikely to derail - Expert
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - A legal expert believes former Defence Minister Nosiviwe Mapisa-Nqakula's corruption trial is unlikely to be marred by postponements.

Melusi Xulu said proceedings should continue as scheduled unless Mapisa-Nqakula's doctors argue otherwise.

“The foundation of a criminal trial, which is based on the Constitution, says there must be a fair trial. So, if you're not feeling well, it's important that the court takes cognisance of that and then you are given time, obviously, to recuperate and be in a better condition. But most possibly a doctor's note will be sufficient,” he said.

Xulu’s comments come as the High Court in Pretoria adjourned its proceedings earlier than expected after Mapisa-Nqakula required medical attention following a full day in the witness stand.

Her lawyer requested an early adjournment, citing Mapisa-Nqakula's fatigue.

READ | Lawyer says Mapisa-Nqakula is 'just tired'

At the time, lawyers attributed the tiredness possibly to the lengthy court process, which can be "gruelling, tiring and frustrating" for someone not used to it.

Xulu said while such an explanation could be valid, a medical proof would be enough for the court to decide if the matter warrants a postponement to a time when she is better state and ready to face the court as directed by the doctor.

Mapisa-Nqakula faces 12 charges of corruption and one of money laundering.

These are linked to allegations that she solicited and received millions of rands in bribes, while serving as Defence Minister.

READ | Mapisa-Nqakula denies 'code words' for alleged bribes

The former minister admitted that defence contractor Nombasa Ntsondwa-Ndhlovu visited her home, but said they discussed a family matter.

She denied soliciting or receiving bribes from Ntsondwa-Ndhlovu.

Mapisa-Nqakula's lawyer said they will await confirmation from the doctors to decide on Thursday's proceedings.

This communication, he said, is expected to happen before the end of the day on Wednesday.

World.title: ODI debutant Hermann scores 150 as Proteas beat Namibia
World.content:
WINDHOEK - Jordan Hermann scored 150 on Wednesday in his one-day international debut for South Africa, which beat Namibia by 99 runs in a rain-shortened first ODI between the countries.

Opener Hermann and Tony de Zorzi put on 190 for the second wicket in Windhoek and the visitors posted 348-6 off 50 overs after being put in to bat.

Rain forced two interruptions to the Namibia reply and, set 262 in 31 overs to win under the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern method, they could only reach 162-8.

It has been a memorable four days for left-hand batter Hermann, whose career-best Twenty20 knock of 53 on Sunday helped South Africa win a tri-series final against Zimbabwe in Namibia.

After fellow opener Connor Esterhuizen fell for 10, Hermann and De Zorzi tormented the Namibian bowlers at one of the venues for the 2027 ODI Men's Cricket World Cup.

Hermann faced 126 deliveries and hit three sixes and 17 fours. The 72 runs of De Zorzi included a six and seven fours.

A soft, lofted shot by Hermann off South Africa-born quick Ruben Trumpelmann proved his undoing as Louren Steenkamp took a catch at extra cover.

De Zorzi was trapped leg before by Gerhard Erasmus after a long appeal and an even longer wait before the umpire raised his finger.

After a 51-run first wicket stand between Malan Kruger (34) and Alexander Busing-Volschenk (15), Namibia battled with spinner Prenelan Subrayen (4-29) inflicting most damage.

Brief scores

South Africa 348-6 in 50 overs (J. Hermann 150, T. de Zorzi 72; R. Trumpelmann 4-68) v Namibia 162-8 in 31 overs (M. Kruger 34, J.J. Smit 31; P. Subrayen 4-29, K. Maphaka 2-32)

Result: South Africa won by 99 runs under the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern method

Toss: Namibia

Series: South Africa lead 1-0 ahead of matches on Friday and Sunday

World.title: Rubio pushes extraditions, anti-drug fight in Ecuador
World.content:
WASHINGTON - US Secretary of State Marco Rubio arrived in Ecuador Wednesday to press the fight against "narco-terrorists" who have transformed the country into one of Latin America's most violent.

Rubio visits Quito as the second stop on a three-nation tour designed to shore up conservative allies in Colombia, Ecuador and Peru, and bolster US influence across the continent.

He is expected to discuss tougher extradition rules for drug traffickers, push military operations against alleged drug-runners and champion investment from politically connected US tech firms like Google, Palantir and SpaceX.

On the eve of his visit, Rubio described Ecuador as "one of our closest security partners in the region, and I think there's more we can do with them."

A year ago, the US government dramatically shifted its anti-drug strategy to include air strikes against vessels suspected of shipping drugs in the Caribbean and the eastern Pacific.

The strikes have killed more than 200 people, according to US Defense Department figures.

World.title: Airports Company South Africa back flying high
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Airports Company South Africa (ACSA) is benefiting from increased travel demand.

The state-owned airport operator, ACSA, which runs nine airports across the country, is showing solid growth.

It's reporting stronger annual earnings as passenger numbers continue to rise.

Growth in both its aviation and commercial businesses has helped lift performance.

Its revenue increased by 11.6% to R8.78 billion.

Passenger numbers are seeing a significant recovery, falling just 2% shy of pre-COVID levels.

However, the one thorn in the side of ACSA's success is jet fuel and labour costs.

These inputs have doubled over the last year.

eNCA senior reporter Aviwe Mtila has filed this report in the video above.

World.title: Mama Tutam acquitted of Sh25m fraud, says Nigerian tycoon cost her marriage
World.content:
Nairobi Woman Representative aspirant Faith Mwikali Ndiwa, alias Faith Nguthu addresses journalists at the Milimani Law Courts in Nairobi on September 9, 2026. [David Gichuru, Standard]

A Nairobi Woman Representative aspirant has confessed the frustrations and embarrassment that befell her after befriending a wealthy Nigerian businessman who later accused her of defrauding him of Sh25 million.

Faith Mwikali Ndiwa, alias Faith Nguthu, popularly known as Mama Tutam, said she was kicked out of her marriage after the father of her three children discovered reports linking her to an alleged love affair with Nigerian investor Jude Olabayo Veracruz.

World.title: Centum taps insider as Mworia exits after nearly two decades
World.content:
Centum Investment Company PLC acting Group Chief Executive Thomas Omondi-Achola. [Courtesy]

Centum Investment Company PLC has appointed Thomas Omondi-Achola as acting group chief executive, tapping an internal candidate to succeed long-serving CEO James Mworia, who is leaving to head Kenya’s newly established National Infrastructure Fund (NIF).

The transition, effective immediately, marks the end of an 18-year tenure during which Mworia transformed Centum from a small investment firm into East Africa’s largest diversified investment platform, the company said in a statement.

World.title: Ruto: Kenya to end raw mineral exports
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto during a thanksgiving service in South Horr, Samburu County on September 6, 2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto says Kenya will no longer allow its mineral wealth to leave the country in raw form, coming days after the controversial saga surrounding Tata Chemicals’ operations at Lake Magadi.

Ruto defended the government’s decision to suspend Tata Chemicals’ operations at Lake Magadi, Kajiado County, arguing that Kenya has not been receiving sufficient value from the natural resource and that more investors should be given an opportunity to develop the area.

“We want to give five, six or even 10 companies an opportunity to use the resources there to create jobs, value, create wealth and reduce poverty,” Ruto said.

The President made the remarks during a thanksgiving service in South Horr, Samburu County, on Sunday, where he announced a broader government policy aimed at shifting Kenya from exporting raw materials to processing them locally.

“Going into the future, our position as the government. Whether we are talking about Magadi Soda or oil or all our minerals, we have taken the decision that we will no longer export raw materials,” Ruto said.

“We are going to process all minerals available in Kenya.”

The declaration puts the long-running Lake Magadi dispute at the centre of a much wider economic strategy.

Tata Chemicals has been associated with soda ash production at the lake for more than a century. Its Kenyan operations trace their history to 1911, when the Magadi Soda Company began extracting trona from Lake Magadi.

Operations were suspended on July 28, 2026, following a directive from the Ministry of Mining, Blue Economy and Maritime Affairs over compliance and licensing issues.

Ruto has argued that the resource should generate greater benefits for Kenyans through expanded investment, job creation and local value addition.

He accused the existing model of allowing valuable resources to leave the country while Kenya receives less economic benefit than it could.

The President’s comments reflect a longstanding challenge facing Kenya’s extractive sector: how to turn mineral deposits into manufacturing opportunities rather than simply exporting commodities.

Under the proposed approach, minerals such as gold, limestone, iron ore, graphite, titanium and soda ash would be processed or refined in Kenya before being exported.

The government says this would create industrial jobs, strengthen local supply chains and increase the value of exports.

Ruto cited planned cooperation with Nigerian businessman Aliko Dangote as an example of the investment model the government wants to pursue.

He said talks were underway to establish an oil refinery and petrochemical complex in Lamu, alongside efforts to attract investors into mineral refining.

“It is imprudent for any government to export raw materials, create jobs and value in other countries while we have a big population of young people who need jobs,” Ruto said.

World.title: Sifuna condemns abduction of Standard Group Associate Editor
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Busia County Senator Okiya Omtata, Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna, Bumula MP Jack Wamboka during the burial service of Mary Gorreti Okiya at Kabula, in Bumula on September 5,2026. [Benjamin Sakwa, Standard]

Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna has declared that the fight to restore democracy, media freedom and the rule of law following the abduction of Standard Group Senior Editor will form the centrepiece of the Linda Mwananchi government vowing to defeat President William Ruto in the 2027 General Election.

Sifuna accused President Ruto’s administration of undermining constitutional freedoms and creating an atmosphere of fear, saying the country must be returned to what he described as “the rail of the six important values” enshrined in the Constitution.

Speaking in Bumula Constituency, Kakamega County during the burial of Mary Goreti, the sister of Busia Senator Okiya Omtatah, Sifuna strongly condemned the abduction and arrest of a Standard Group Associate Editor, Alex Kiprotich, arguing that journalists must be protected if Kenya is to remain a democratic country.

“It is impossible that you are driving on the road and you are taken away the way the way the Standard Group Journaliat and Editor Alex Kiprotich was taken. Kenyans want to live in a free country. We do not want to live in fear,” said Sifuna.

He questioned the circumstances surrounding the incident and accused the Government of failing to protect media freedom, adding that the Linda Mwananchi movement would seek to restore institutions and constitutional safeguards if elected to power, arguing that democracy could not survive where citizens, journalists and political opponents lived in fear.

"You cannot just arrest a senior journalist in the middle of the road with police carrying firearms, then you dump him some 500kilometres near the dam, a country cannot have democracy if media is not being respected and allowed to do it's work as per the constitution," said Sifuna.

He said the movement’s agenda was not merely about removing the current administration from power but it's main plan is rebuilding systems of governance around constitutionalism, democracy, individual freedoms and the rule of law.

“With less than 11 months remaining, we want to tell Kenyans that our entire plan is to return this country to the rails of the six important values contained in our Constitution, including democracy, freedom of citizens and the rule of law,” said Sifuna.

Sifuna also accused the Government of using threats against political opponents, saying leaders should not threaten citizens with arrest, expulsion or other forms of intimidation.

He challenged religious leaders to remind politicians that the power to determine the length of a person's life belongs to God.

Sifuna further linked the rule of law to economic growth, warning that investors would be reluctant to establish businesses in Kenya if government could arbitrarily order them to leave.

He said Kenya could not rely on government alone to create employment for millions of young people, arguing that the country needed both local and foreign investors.

“No investor can bring his project to a country where he can wake up one day and the President tells him, ‘Pack and go.’ It is impossible,” Sifuna said.

He argued that investor confidence was also affected by the possibility of commercial disputes being referred to foreign jurisdictions because investors lacked confidence in Kenya’s legal system.

Sifuna also criticised the government over the ongoing nurses and midwives strike, saying the rule of law required the State to honour agreements signed with workers.

World.title: Murkomen reaffirms IG Kanja's command of National Police Service
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen has reaffirmed that the Inspector General of Police retains constitutional command of the National Police Service, saying the government will continue to respect the independence of the office.

Speaking during the passing-out parade of new Administration Police recruits in Nairobi, Murkomen said the Inspector General has authority over key operational matters within the service, including investigations, promotions and deployment of officers.

“Your Excellency, the Inspector General of Police retains the command of the National Police Service, especially on matters of investigation, promotion and deployment of officers without interference from anyone, including the Cabinet Secretary. We will continue respecting Article 245 of the Constitution,” Murkomen said.

His remarks come amid public debate over the relationship between the Interior Ministry and the National Police Service, particularly allegations that political leaders sometimes issue direct instructions to police officers.

Murkomen dismissed criticism directed at the office of the Inspector General, describing some of its proponents as tribalists and propagandists. He maintained that the Inspector General is carrying out his responsibilities and said he had confidence in the leadership of the police service.

“I have full faith in the IG and believe that every act that is done by the National Police Service is guided by the Constitution,” he said.

The Cabinet Secretary also addressed concerns over his role in directing the police, saying that his responsibility is primarily to provide policy direction rather than interfere with the operational command of the service.

“When required to give policy direction, I always give it in writing and we will continue to support the independence of the National Police Service from external interference,” Murkomen said.

During the ceremony, Murkomen also cautioned the newly graduated officers against corruption, excessive alcohol consumption and conduct that could undermine the reputation of the police service.

He urged the recruits to uphold discipline and protect the dignity of the police uniform, noting that the respect they receive from members of the public would depend largely on their conduct.

The Cabinet Secretary encouraged the officers to understand the responsibility that comes with joining the National Police Service and to discharge their duties within the confines of the Constitution and the law.

The passing-out ceremony marked the entry of the new recruits into the police service that made the CS use the occasion to emphasize professional conduct and respect for the constitutional framework governing policing in Kenya.

World.title: Ruto assures Kajiado residents of full control of Amboseli National Park
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto inspects the Rombo Clusters Irrigation Development Project in Kajiado County on September 3, 2026. [Peterson Githaiga, Standard]

President William Ruto has assured Kajiado residents that they will soon have full control of the management of Amboseli National Park, following his decision to return the park to the county in November 2025.

However, he said the transfer has been temporarily halted by the court.

The President hit out at those he accused of frustrating the move, saying they will be in for a rude shock.

“They took us to court over the Social Health Authority and the Affordable Housing Programme, but these programmes are progressing well. Similarly, I want to assure the people of Kajiado that, before the end of this year, Amboseli will be fully in the hands of Kajiado County,” he said.

Speaking in Kajiado County on Thursday during his development tour, President Ruto reiterated that he will not relent in his pursuit of equity and inclusive development across Kenya, saying that longstanding inequalities have unduly benefited certain regions at the expense of others.

He revealed that the securitisation of the Road Maintenance Levy Fund and the Sports Fund has enabled the Government to clear pending bills in the roads sector and construct 6,000km of new roads, and accelerate the construction of 32 new stadia across the country.

"The Road Maintenance Levy Fund was misused to only build roads in some parts of the country. Those opposing securitisation are unhappy that we are advancing equity," he said.

The President began his tour at Oloirien in Kajiado South Constituency by inspecting progress of the 67km Illasit-Rombo-Chala-Njukini-Taveta road, which is 48 per cent completed.

The Sh9.4 billion project will cut travel time between Kajiado and Taita-Taveta counties from two hours to just 40 minutes, thus easing the movement of goods and people.

The Head of State announced that eight new roads of 220km are being built across Kajiado County at a cost of Sh13 billion to open up the region and improve transport.

The President commissioned Sh221 million Rombo Clusters Irrigation Development Project, which is expected to enhance livelihoods and boost irrigation in the area.

He also inspected progress of the Sh2.2 billion Loitoktok Affordable Housing Project, and laid the foundation stone for the Sh220 million Loitoktok Kenya Medical Training College student hostels with a 580-bed capacity.

At Kimana, in Kajiado South Constituency, President Ruto commissioned the Sh2.7 billion Sultan Hamud-Loitoktok 132kV Transmission Line and Loitoktok Sub-Station, which will serve the residents of Kajiado South and parts of Makueni County.

He inspected construction of the Kimana modern market, which is aimed at giving traders dignified working environment.

At Namanga, Kajiado Central Constituency, the President commissioned the Namanga Sub-Station, a project of the Kenya Electricity Transmission Company (KETRACO), which is part of the 132KV Machakos- Konza-Isinya-Namanga Transmission Project.

Namanga Modern Market, which is under construction at a cost of Sh50 million, will benefit 120 traders at the border town.

In Kajiado town, the President toured the construction of the Kajiado Affordable Housing Project, a Sh473 million investment that will deliver 196 housing units, as well as the 100-unit police housing project at a cost of Sh137 million.

He also inspected the progress of the 580-bed student hostels at Maasai National Polytechnic, which is being built at a cost of KSh216 million.

Ruto ordered the closer of Tata Chemicals, saying the government will identify a new and responsible investor to take over soda ash mining operations at Lake Magadi.

The President said Tata Chemicals had failed to adequately modernise the plant, create sufficient employment opportunities for residents, and deliver meaningful economic benefits to the people of Kenya.

“It is unfair for one company to dominate the ownership and operations of Magadi Soda for years, yet it has done little to improve the factory or create employment opportunities for our youth,” he said at Rombo in Kajiado South Constituency.

He added: “Because they have been unable to do anything meaningful with the plant for more than 100 years, I have directed them to pack up and go.”

The Ministry of Mining suspended the company’s mining operations in July 2026 over concerns relating to regulatory compliance, value addition and licensing.

The ministry also ordered the closure of the company’s depot in Kajiado Town for contravening environmental regulations.

In addition, the company has been unable to reach an agreement with the Kajiado County Government over a land rates dispute following the expiry of its operating licence in 2023.

The plant produces soda ash, or sodium carbonate, a key industrial mineral used in the manufacture of glass, soap and laundry detergents, among other products.

Despite being Africa’s largest soda ash producer, President Ruto noted that the operation had not delivered commensurate benefits to Kenyans over its more than 100-year history, particularly because much of the soda ash produced is exported for processing and consumption in overseas markets.

The Government, the President said, would therefore prioritise an investor capable of modernising the facility, expanding local value addition, creating jobs for young people, and ensuring that Kenya derives greater economic value from its natural resources.

World.title: IG Kanja orders probe into abduction of Standard Group Associate Editor
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Standard Group PLC Associate Editor Alex Kiprotich. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

The Inspector General of Police Douglas Kanja has ordered immediate and transparent investigations into the alleged abduction of Standard Group Associate Editor Alex Kiprotich in Gilgil.

The National Police Service (NPS) said it had taken note of reports that Kiprotich was allegedly kidnapped on Tuesday and had moved swiftly to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident.

NPS spokesperson Muchiri Nyaga said the police service treats kidnapping and abduction with the utmost seriousness, describing the offences as a threat to the lives, liberty and security of Kenyans.

“The Inspector General of Police has accordingly ordered immediate investigations to determine what transpired, including the identity of the heavily armed individuals reportedly seen ordering occupants out of their vehicle,” Nyaga said in a statement.

The NPS said its Anti-Abduction Unit, established to investigate abductions and disappearances, had taken up the matter and would work to ensure that those responsible are brought to justice.

“We unequivocally condemn any act of kidnapping, abduction, or intimidation intended to interfere with press freedom or any other constitutional right,” Nyaga said.

The police service assured the public that the investigation into the Gilgil incident would be conducted transparently, stressing that no one was above the law.

The development comes amid growing condemnation of Kiprotich’s alleged abduction, with the Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) also calling for an immediate investigation.

CPJ Africa Director Angela Quintal described the incident as a “shameful indictment” of the Kenya Kwanza administration, raising concerns over the safety of journalists and press freedom in the country.

“The attempt to forcibly disappear Alex Kiprotich, three days after President William Ruto railed against The Standard Group, reflects the growing dangers that journalists face in Kenya, despite the president’s earlier promise to allow the press to work freely,” Quintal said.

The New York-based press freedom organisation further expressed concern over what it described as an escalation in cases of abductions and enforced disappearances in Kenya.

World.title: Trumpets of reforms blow louder as Kenya marks 16 years under 2010 Constitution
World.content:
The Constitution, Kenyan flag and the National anthem. [PCS]

On Thursday, August 27, a group of people largely composed of the youth gathered under some trees at Jeevanjee Gardens in Nairobi, carrying Kenyans flag, and banners and placards inscribed with "implement the constitution. Kenyans first" words.

These were in protests against what they believed is deliberate failure of those in authority to fully implement the 2010 Constitution.

World.title: Trump lays out next moves after Canada’s retaliatory tariffs take effect
World.content:
New York — The trade war between the United States and Canada has entered a new chapter — and it’s getting uglier by the hour.

Early Tuesday morning, Canada made good on its promise to impose tariffs on $20 billion worth of American goods in retaliation for the Canadian goods President Donald Trump began taxing last month.

Less than 24 hours after those levies went into effect, Trump unveiled his next move to exert more pressure on Ottawa.

Now, tariffs are no longer the only weapon of choice: Trump is prepared to enact outright bans on a slew of Canadian goods. He also threatened to prevent the US government from buying Canadian-made products through a major federal purchasing program unless Canada gives American companies and farmers greater access to its markets.

Canada’s Prime Minister Mark Carney has previously vowed “dollar-for-dollar” retaliation and is all but certain to respond to Trump if he moves forward with his threats.

That includes effectively barring Americans from importing a wide range of Canadian-made alcoholic beverages, motorcycles and whey. The ban will take effect on September 29 at 12:01 a.m. ET, according to materials published by the White House on Tuesday evening. Until then, many of the products will be subject to 50 percent duties.

Trump also expanded the list of products subject to those levies, including golf carts, drawing paper and more steel and aluminum parts.

Trade talks between the two neighbors, which have been top trading partners for close to half a century, broke down last month at the 11th hour. Trump had initially pushed back his self-imposed deadline for the tariffs, touting a deal that was within reach. But the two sides failed to bridge their remaining differences as negotiators haggled over the final details.

Since then, Trump and Carney have traded increasingly pointed jabs. Trump went as far as renaming Lake Ontario as “Lake America,” a move that Canadians and even some Republicans oppose. He also threatened to double auto tariffs to 50 percent starting next year and plans to ban one of Canada’s top aircraft companies, Bombardier, from selling in the US unless it manufactures them there.

In a response to CNN, the Montreal-based company said it maintains a significant manufacturing presence in the US and has continued to expand in the country. “The American aerospace industry is a clear winner on trade and exports. Bombardier is a strong contributor to the sector, creating tens of thousands of jobs across the United States,” it said.

Canada’s Prime Minister Mark Carney walks to speak with the news media in Ottawa on August 22. Chris Tanouye/Reuters

Throughout the trade talks, Carney has accused the Americans of not negotiating seriously.

“When the Americans stop doing memes, stop throwing shade, stop trying to be tough and start being serious about having those discussions — we can have those discussions,” Carney said last week.

The intensifying trade war between the two neighbors is unfolding just two months before the US midterm elections, putting Republicans in competitive races in the position of explaining their views on tariffs imposed by the president. That includes Sen. Susan Collins of Maine, who faces a tough reelection fight and has criticized Trump’s tariffs.

Canadian Minister of Industry Mélanie Joly said the government is specifically tailoring its countermeasures to “put political pressure” on the Trump administration to reconsider its actions. Ottawa, however, exempted American seafood from the 25 percent duties — a move that spared industries in key states such as Alaska and Maine from a potentially significant hit.

For Americans, this next tit-for-tat could hit closer to home.

Ontario Premier Doug Ford has said that his province could put restrictions on electricity exports to the border states it supplies, such as New York and Michigan.

Why talks broke down

Canadian officials said their American counterparts pressed Canada to change rules governing how prominently Canadian and French-language content is displayed on streaming platforms, as well as product labeling requirements for English and French. Carney has defended those protections as fundamental to Canadian culture.

“For the Americans, questions about the French language, Quebec culture, francophone culture and Canadian culture are irritants. Here in Quebec, here in Canada, they are rights, fundamental rights,” Carney said last month.

Trump, meanwhile, said, “I would never interfere with Canadians speaking French!” He added in a Truth Social post that he viewed Carney’s stance toward the US as an attempt to strengthen his political base.

A banner celebrating Canadian-United States cooperation hangs outside the Canadian Embassy on August 26 in Washington, DC. Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images

US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer has denied that discussions over French-language requirements were the cause of the collapsed talks.

Carney portrayed that as a reversal from the discussions that took place. “All of a sudden, they don’t care about Canadian language or culture and those elements. Well, if they didn’t care, they shouldn’t have kept them in the deal,” Carney said last week.

US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick said the deal fell apart because of last-minute requests Canadian trade officials made, including tariff relief for trucks. The US currently imposes a 25 percent duty on those vehicles, with exemptions for the portion of each vehicle that complies with the trilateral trade agreement between the US, Canada and Mexico that Trump brokered during his first term. The same 25 percent duties apply to cars and car parts.

As part of the preliminary deal, the US had agreed to lower auto tariffs to 15 percent, “with the possibility of going down to 7 percent,” Greer said in an August interview with CBC News. He also said that they agreed to halve levies on steel and aluminum to 25 percent.

Who has the upper hand?

On the sidelines of the G20 meeting of finance ministers and central bankers last week, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent suggested America has the upper hand in the trade war. “I don’t think you can be in a tit-for-tat with someone who’s 13 times larger than you are,” he said in a CNBC interview on August 31.

While it’s true that the US economy is 13 times the size of Canada’s in terms of gross domestic product last year, that doesn’t mean the US can walk away unscathed.

However, Trump on Friday said the US would save money by cutting off trade with Canada. “If we don’t do any trading with Canada, we just end all trade with Canada, we’d save ourselves $90 billion.”

That’s not exactly true: The US-Canadian trade relationship is such that both sides rely on each other for goods that can’t easily be substituted from other trading partners, multiplying the pain both sides feel, irrespective of the size of their economies.

In general, when a trade war breaks out, the smaller economy has more to lose compared to the larger one, said Ari Van Assche, a professor of international business at HEC Montréal who specializes in international trade. That’s because bigger economies tend to rely less on trade to access goods and services compared to smaller economies.

Take, for instance, Ford’s automotive factory in Windsor, Canada, which produces specialized engines for some of the American manufacturer’s biggest trucks.

“It’s difficult for (Ford) to say, ‘Ah, no problem. We’re going to import it now from Mexico,’ because the components made in Mexico are very different,” Van Assche told CNN.

Since businesses often negotiate pricing contracts well in advance of when goods reach ports, consumers on both sides of the border are unlikely to see immediate effects of the new duties, said Gordon Hanson, a professor at Harvard University’s Kennedy School who studies trade and immigration.

But, by next summer, they could see markedly higher prices.

This story has been updated.

World.title: How Trump has failed to learn the lessons of the wars that followed 9/11
World.content:
Friday marks the 25th anniversary of the attacks of September 11, 2001. Since 9/11, US presidents have expanded their power, step by step, to wage war anywhere, anytime, as they please.

With Operation Epic Fury in Iran, President Donald Trump reached a new peak in the war-making powers claimed by the US commander in chief. Trump launched his war of choice on Iran — in his words, “the world’s No. 1 state sponsor of terror” — without any congressional authorization, the support of NATO allies or a UN resolution. There was also scant buy-in from the American public for what was at its outset the least popular war of the modern era, nor was there anything resembling an imminent threat to the United States. Nor had Trump bothered to learn anything from past American wars, and he did not have a real plan for the “day after” hostilities commenced.

The US military has long been adept at breaking things and killing people, but when its tactics were not aligned with a clear strategy, the United States ended up in the quagmire of Vietnam, or the sectarian civil war in Iraq that eventually birthed ISIS, or precipitating a possible global economic recession caused by the Iran war.

Trump’s predecessors also laid the groundwork for the Iran war. The “war on terror” morphed over time in the months after 9/11, beyond the war in Afghanistan against the Taliban and al Qaeda that was backed by the UN and NATO allies. It then grew to encompass President George W. Bush’s doctrine of “preventive war” that justified the 2003 invasion of Iraq. That invasion led to a civil war during which an estimated 200,000 Iraqi civilians died.

The war on terror expanded to include President Barack Obama’s prolific use of armed drones in countries such as Pakistan and Yemen that were not at war with the United States; attacks that killed thousands of suspected terrorists and a sizeble number of civilians.

Pakistani victims of a US drone attack rest on a bed after they arrived in Peshawar on November 3, 2012. A Majeed/AFP/Getty Images

With UN and NATO support, Obama also ordered the campaign to remove the Libyan dictator Moammar Gadhafi from power in 2011, but Obama didn’t seek approval from Congress. The overthrow of Gadhafi precipitated a civil war in Libya that lasted a decade, and the country continues to be divided, ruled today by two governments. Obama later said that not planning for the “day after” Gadhafi’s fall was his greatest failure as president.

During the “global war on terror,” the United States cycled through a variety of strategies and tactics, some of which backfired spectacularly. Those include Bush’s Iraq invasion and the bipartisan fiasco of the US withdrawal from Afghanistan more than a decade and a half later, an agreement negotiated under Trump and executed under President Joe Biden.

The US pullout from Afghanistan predictably resulted in the Taliban taking over the country. The debacles of the Iraq War and the Afghanistan withdrawal signaled that the US superpower had little idea what it was doing when it came to foreign policy, which undercut its position around the world.

There were some real American operational successes during the war on terror: The CIA became an effective paramilitary agency hunting and killing terrorists; Joint Special Operations Command transformed from a barely used counterterrorism force to an industrial-level killing machine; US Special Forces partnered adeptly with Afghan and Iraqi ground forces; and the National Security Agency skillfully penetrated enemy communications.

All these developments played important roles in eventually decimating the leadership of al Qaeda and ending the geographical “caliphate” of ISIS. As a result, there were no large-scale lethal attacks by foreign terrorist groups in the United States following 9/11, which was a major national security goal of the four post-9/11 presidents.

Last fall, Trump dramatically expanded the ambit of the war on terror when he claimed that he could kill suspected Latin American drug cartel members at will on the grounds that they were “narcoterrorists.” This resulted in dozens of American strikes on boats transporting drugs in the Caribbean, and when US Joint Special Operations Command captured Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro in early 2026, Trump asserted he was a narcoterrorist.

Encouraged by what he termed the “brilliant” operation to remove Maduro from power, Trump soon issued the order for Operation Epic Fury. This echoed the way the relatively quick war to overthrow the Taliban after 9/11 emboldened Bush to launch the war on Iraq a year and half later.

A lesson that the United States never learned after 9/11: Make real plans for the “day after” the war appears to be won, or you will likely lose the peace. The Bush administration didn’t negotiate a peace agreement with the Taliban until after the group was utterly defeated in December 2001 when many of its leaders were looking to cut a deal, which could have avoided many years of war. The many failures to plan for what followed the fall of Saddam Hussein’s regime in Iraq were well known, and yet only eight years later the Obama administration also made no plan for what happened after the overthrow of Gadhafi.

Iraqi civilians and US soldiers pull down a statue of Saddam Hussein in downtown Baghdad on April 9, 2003. Jerome Delay/AP

The confusion about what constituted American strategic success and merely tactical US wins was particularly evident during the Iran war when the many military victories against the theocrats in Tehran did not produce any meaningful change in the regime. As Trump himself admitted during the first days of the conflict: “You go through this, and then in five years you realize you put somebody in who’s no better.”

This grim prediction would come true in only a matter of weeks. The United States’ dismal record of regime changes in the post-9/11 Middle East also did not inspire confidence that America’s regime decapitation project in Iran would have a happy ending. Meanwhile, the Iranian regime has wielded its newfound control of the Strait of Hormuz to inject great turmoil into the gas and oil markets that fuel the global economy.

Twenty-five years after 9/11, the United States, which once prided itself on being the guarantor of global order, is now its chief disruptor.

World.title: ‘Surge in construction’ at suspected Iranian nuclear site, analysts say, as US considers ways to strike deep underground
World.content:
A suspected Iranian nuclear site buried under granite has seen a flurry of construction work this year as the war with the US has transpired, according to a group of analysts who reviewed six years of satellite imagery.

The Pickaxe Mountain site, located near the Natanz nuclear complex roughly 140 miles south of Tehran, has been the subject of steady discussion by intelligence agencies which view it as a likely location for Iran to protect future nuclear program efforts.

According to a new satellite imagery analysis by the Center for Strategic and International Studies think tank, shared exclusively with CNN ahead of its publication, there has been “a clear surge in construction activity” this year.

The underground facility is “likely” designed to be a safe haven for Iran’s nuclear program, according to the CSIS analysts.

Israeli intelligence has suggested that Iran may be seeking to move centrifuges to the location as part of uranium enrichment efforts, and President Donald Trump has repeatedly threatened to strike the site.

“We may hit Pickaxe very soon,” Trump told reporters last week, adding that “we know everybody that’s moving” at the site.

The granite mountain, however, presents a difficult target to even the Pentagon’s “heaviest non-nuclear” bombs, the CSIS team reported. And It’s not the only Iranian nuclear facility feared to be out of reach for current-generation weapons.

But there are signs the US is working to devise some means of striking those sites, even as US forces have largely focused on other types of targets during the six-month conflict with Iran.

Four days before the US launched Operation Epic Fury, a program manager at an obscure Pentagon agency charged with combating weapons of mass destruction signed an emergency $1.2 million contract justification to repair a “unique subterranean test facility at White Sands Missile Range” in New Mexico for a “live-fire test designed to validate classified capabilities against rapidly emerging threats.”

The document from the Defense Threat Reduction Agency was uploaded to a federal database on February 27 — the day before the war started.

The memo said the “rapid test prep,” as another database labeled the contract awarded to Pate Construction, needed to be complete within two-to-three weeks due to “a time-sensitive national security directive.”

The plans for the test were connected to the Iran war, three sources familiar with the matter told CNN, and the need to develop a way to target Iran’s deepest-buried underground facilities and, likely, simulate US strikes against specific nuclear facilities.

The US previously struck nuclear sites in June 2025 as part of what the military called Operation Midnight Hammer. While the strikes successfully destroyed some key locations linked to Tehran’s nuclear program, a top US general told lawmakers last year that the deeply buried Isfahan nuclear site only had its entrances buried because the Pentagon believed its bunker-busting bombs — known as the Massive Ordnance Penetrator — could not knock it out.

The military is working to develop a “next generation penetrator” bomb to succeed the current MOP and potentially hit targets even more deeply buried. A contract to begin work on a prototype was awarded in September 2025, and the Air Force solicited defense industry sources for the new weapon in June.

Satellite imagery reviewed by CNN shows that between February 16 and February 18, excavation work began at a remote DTRA and US Strategic Command-operated site at White Sands intended to test the effects of weapons on deeply buried targets. The timing aligns with that of the emergency contract: Pate Construction provided an estimate for the test work on February 17 and received the deal the next day, according to federal contracting records.

Work at the remote location, known as the Alternate Seismic Hardrock in Situ Test Site, continued into mid-March as a pile of excavation dirt gradually grew. The round of activity appeared to halt then, according to the imagery.

Similar to Pickaxe Mountain, the DTRA test site in White Sands is also carved into granite, according to an environmental assessment.

CNN could not independently verify whether the test occurred, nor could CNN confirm the purpose of the work at the DTRA test site observed via satellite imagery. The Pentagon did not immediately reply to questions from CNN. Pate Construction did not return calls from a CNN reporter.

The US military maintains operational plans for strikes against Pickaxe, and it was part of a target package that was under consideration earlier this summer when Trump was threatening to escalate the conflict with Iran, according to a source familiar with the matter. The strike plan for Pickaxe involved using some of the largest bombs in the US arsenal, though it remains unclear if those munitions can penetrate deep enough underground to destroy whatever Iran may have moved there, the source added.

Efforts to develop plans for decisive strikes against underground facilities continue; a source familiar with the matter told CNN that elements within the Defense Department recently held a “planning sprint” on the topic.

The facility at Pickaxe Mountain is “likely” designed for one of three purposes, all related to Iran’s nuclear program, according to the CSIS analysis. It could be a centrifuge assembly facility, an enrichment facility, or a safe haven for other “nuclear weapons-relevant” work such as uranium metal conversion.

In their report, the CSIS analysts argued the construction at the site “has shifted from active excavation toward probably internal construction and continued exterior reinforcement.” Pickaxe Mountain in 2026 has seen “more road activity” than ever before, and additional work has included “raising and hardening of the (tunnel) portal accesses, paving of the internal road network, reinforcement around access areas, and the flattening and removal” of dirt excavated while building its tunnels, the report said.

The CSIS analysts cautioned that the “continuous construction” they’ve observed at Pickaxe Mountain, among other factors, suggests the site “is not yet capable of enrichment work, if that is the intended purpose.”

CNN’s Tal Shalev contributed to this report.

Davis Winkie’s work at CNN is supported by a partnership between Outrider Foundation and Journalism Funding Partners (JFP). CNN retains full editorial control of the reporting.

World.title: US claims Chinese AI firms are carrying out ‘industrial-scale’ theft of trade secrets
World.content:
Chinese artificial intelligence firms are committing “industrial-scale” theft of their American counterparts’ trade secrets to save money and bring the coveted technology to market faster, US federal agencies alleged Tuesday.

Major Chinese tech companies are using “distillation,” which involves training lesser AI models on more advanced ones, to “extract restricted proprietary functionalities and capabilities of U.S. frontier AI models,” the FBI, National Security Agency, and Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency claimed in an advisory.

Distillation can be a legitimate research technique, but American officials and AI executives have long complained that the volume and targeted manner of Chinese distillation campaigns against US firms amount to stealing. The new advisory puts more evidence behind those accusations and adds to the growing tensions between US and China over AI technology. President Donald Trump has said that AI will be among the discussion topics when he hosts Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Washington, DC, later this month

“The sheer scale of these campaigns and their sophistication indicate that distillation is not a supplement to these companies’ AI model development, but the critical core of it,” the new advisory says.

China-based AI firms “use a gray market of proxies known as ‘transfer stations’” to get around US AI firms’ geographic restrictions, safeguards, and terms of use, the US agencies said. They singled out several Chinese tech firms, including DeepSeek and Alibaba Group, as having conducted “high-volume knowledge distillation campaigns” against US AI firms.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent threatened sanctions against Chinese companies that distill American AI.

“When [People’s Republic of China] firms conduct covert, industrial-scale distillation attacks that cross the line into IP theft, sanctions and Entity List designations will be on the table,” he wrote on X.

“The U.S. side’s hyping of the so-called ‘distillation’ concept is deliberate attack on China’s development and progress in the AI industry. China firmly rejects it,” a spokesperson for the Chinese Embassy in Washington, DC, said in a statement.

On Wednesday, China’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said China’s AI development reflected its high level of self-reliance and strength in science and technology. The US, she said, should refrain from making “unfounded accusations against or smearing China.”

“China and the United States are both major powers in artificial intelligence and should strengthen cooperation,” Mao said.

CNN has requested comment from DeepSeek and Alibaba.

Anthropic alleged that three Chinese AI labs had been behind an “industrial-scale campaign” to extract capabilities from Anthropic’s AI model, Claude. The Chinese labs “generated over 16 million exchanges with Claude through approximately 24,000 fraudulent accounts,” Anthropic claimed.

Chinese open-weight AI models are growing in popularity since they are highly customizable, can operate off the cloud and tend to be less expensive.

The global race for AI supremacy has put a bull’s-eye on American firms in other ways. Hackers of various stripes are “increasingly targeting AI assets,” Google’s Threat Intelligence Group said in a report released Tuesday.

Hackers with a range of motivations have targeted “proprietary AI models and source code,” the report said. “This shift underscores that enterprise AI assets—from model weights to cloud compute quotas—are high-value targets for espionage, extortion, and resource theft.”

This story has been updated with additional information.

CNN’s Hadas Gold and John Liu contributed to this report.

World.title: Three western nations move to ban imports of Israeli products from West Bank settlements
World.content:
Britain, France, and Canada on Tuesday announced measures to ban imports of goods originating from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank.

The three nations said that this aims to support the two-state solution amidst growing international concern over settlement expansion, Reuters reported.

The move comes part of a series of measures against Israel’s settlement policy, and follows as ten other countries have joined a joint statement affirming their commitment to protecting the two-state solution and pursuing a just and lasting peace through negotiations.

British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said that his country could no longer simply condemn what he described as injustice and suffering, emphasizing the need to take action against settlement expansion—a practice he views as a threat to the viability of a future Palestinian state.

Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand affirmed that settlements in the West Bank undermine efforts to achieve a long-lasting peace based on the two-state solution.

And France said that the acceleration of settlement expansion and escalating violence in the West Bank forced it to take this step.

Backlash from Israel and the US

These measures drew criticism from Israel and the US.

Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich called for the expulsion of the British ambassador, while National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir demanded the closure of the British consulate in East Jerusalem.

These moves coincided with Israel’s announcement of plans to build 1,000 new housing units in the West Bank, amidst growing international concern regarding the “E1” settlement project near Jerusalem—a project viewed one of the most significant threats to the territorial contiguity of Palestinian lands.

Although settlement exports account for only a small fraction of Israel’s total trade, the bans carry political and diplomatic significance, forming part of broader efforts to press for the preservation of the two-state solution.

World.title: Egypt, Kekkilä-BVB review plans for alternative soil factory in SCZone
World.content:
Egypt is exploring the establishment of a local factory to produce alternative soil, aiming to cut imports, lower agricultural production costs and support the expansion of modern, high-value farming and agri-exports.

Industry Minister Khaled Hashem had talks with Pekka Tennilä, CEO of Kekkilä-BVB, on the company’s plan to establish a factory in Egypt in partnership with Egyptian agritech company Agriventure. The facility is planned for the Suez Canal Economic Zone and will produce alternative growing soil for precision farming.

Hashem said localizing alternative growing-soil production is a strategic priority for supporting modern and protected agriculture and increasing value added in agro-industrial manufacturing.

He added that agricultural manufacturing technologies are among the ministry’s priorities for linking scientific research with industrial outputs, meeting export requirements, reducing production costs and narrowing the import gap.

The minister also highlighted the importance of deploying advanced technologies and innovative solutions across productive activities, particularly those that help conserve water and improve resource efficiency in agriculture.

Such solutions, he said, can support the growth and competitiveness of agro-industrial projects and strengthen their export potential.

Kekkilä-BVB company officials said alternative growing media account for around 30% of the cost of precision farming, underscoring the importance of local production in reducing agricultural costs. The planned factory will serve the domestic market while expanding exports to European, African and Arab markets.

Hashem also said Agriventure could participate in the ministry’s “Productive Village” initiative, particularly in villages with a competitive edge in medicinal and aromatic plants and export-oriented crops.

The initiative aims to support balanced industrial development and curb illegal migration and population movement from the regions by leveraging the comparative advantages of each governorate and village. It includes providing small industrial workshops and complexes, concessional financing for small investors, and technical support to connect small businesses with medium- and large-scale factories and strengthen supply-chain integration.

The minister added that Egypt’s industrial map will help identify the comparative advantages of each village and potentially allocate sites for precision-farming projects, particularly in villages known for producing medicinal and aromatic plants and export-oriented crops.

World.title: Egypt, Dubai chambers discuss boosting joint investments
World.content:
CEO of the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) Mohamed Awad, and CEO of Dubai Chambers Mohamed Ali Rashed Lootah discussed on Tuesday, September 8, 2026, ways to enhance economic and investment cooperation and support partnerships between Egypt and the UAE.

The meeting, attended by Head of the Egyptian Trade Representation Office in the UAE Manal Abdel Tawab, came as part of efforts to strengthen economic and investment ties between the two countries and expand cooperation between their business communities.

Awad highlighted the role of Dubai Chambers in connecting businesses with global markets, referring to the potential to activate its Cairo office to promote investment opportunities in Egypt among Emirati companies and support those seeking to expand in the Egyptian market.

He pointed to opportunities for new projects and partnerships in manufacturing, logistics, renewable energy, technology, tourism, real estate development, and supply-chain-related manufacturing and re-export.

Lootah stressed the importance of continued coordination between Dubai Chambers and GAFI to promote investment opportunities and create new avenues for Egyptian-Emirati partnerships and joint projects.

World.title: Cataract beneficiary praises government
World.content:
The Ministry of Health has commenced a one-week eye screening and free cataract‑surgery exercise in Siavonga District aimed at improving access to eye‑care services in the area.

The exercise, which is being conducted at Siavonga District Hospital and selected health facilities, is targeting people with various eye conditions with particular emphasis on cataracts.

Speaking during the launch of the exercise, Lead Ophthalmologist Juliet Mulenga said early detection and treatment of eye problems is critical in preventing permanent blindness.

Dr Mulenga encouraged members of the public, especially the elderly, to take advantage of the free services being offered during the campaign.

One of the beneficiaries, a 57-year-old Virginia Masalabanda of Kabbyobyo in Simamba Ward, who had been unable to see with her left eye due to cataracts for a period of nine months, expressed gratitude to the government and the medical team for restoring her sight.

She also encouraged people experiencing similar eye problems to visit the hospital regularly, adding that the surgery procedures are not as complicated as many believe, and urged affected individuals to seek help so they can recover.

And Siavonga District Senior Nursing Officer in Charge, Agrippa Mudenda, said the hospital is ready to attend to all patients who come for screening during the week.

He said the ministry is providing free services such as comprehensive eye examinations, vision testing, refraction, cataract screening and identification, as well as free cataract surgery for eligible patients.

Mr Mudenda pointed out that the outreach is part of the government’s commitment to decongest hospitals and bring specialised eye‑care services closer to communities across the district.

He noted that myths surrounding cataracts and other eye conditions are not true, and urged residents to ignore such misconceptions and take advantage of the free eye‑screening services instead of waiting for their conditions to worsen before seeking medical attention.

World.title: Judgment in theft case scheduled for September 16
World.content:
The Chisamba Magistrates’ Court has set September 16, 2026, as judgment day for a 25 year‑old man accused of stealing assorted property valued at 33,000 kwacha from his employer.

Moonga Mwendalabi, a caretaker of Chipande Village in Chief Liteta’s area, pleaded not guilty to one count of theft by servant when he appeared before Resident Magistrate Susan Magalashi.

The offence is contrary to Sections 272 and 278 of the Penal Code, Chapter 87 of the Laws of Zambia.

Particulars of the offence are that between April 4, 2026, and July 11, 2026, Mr Mwendalabi, being an employee of Ngonga Kayela and acting jointly with other persons unknown, allegedly stole 53 standard poles X 1.8 metres, three rolls of water drip lines, and two car batteries.

Other items allegedly stolen include 4 X 90 kilogram bags of soya beans, 30 X 50 kilogram bags of maize and 3 X 50 kilogram bags of fertilizer, all valued at 33, 000 kwacha belonging to his employer.

When the matter came up for a ruling after four witnesses called by the prosecution testified, Magistrate Magalashi found Mr Mwendalabi with a case to answer and placed him on his defence.

During his defence, Mr Mwendalabi gave sworn testimony but did not call any witness.

In his defence, Mr Mwendalabi maintained his denial, saying he had nothing to do with the alleged theft and that he left everything intact when he left the farm.

Mr Mwendalabi said he was surprised when police officers picked him up and detained him at Kabwata Police Station in Lusaka for several days before transferring him to Chisamba Police Station.

“I don’t know anything since I left everything intact at the farm. And I was very surprised to see police coming to pick me up and detain me at Kabwata Police Station for eight days before transferring me to Chisamba police station,” Mwendalabi said

After hearing his defence, Magistrate Magalashi adjourned the matter to September 16, 2026, for judgment, while Mr Mwendalabi remains in police custody.

World.title: Choma Police detain suspect in fatal stabbing
World.content:
A 33‑year‑old woman of Choma’s Zambia Compound has been found dead in her marital home.

According to police, the deceased, identified as Rosemary Mudenda, was found lying in a pool of blood with a knife near her head, believed to have been used in the incident.

Southern Province Commissioner of Police, Moono Namalongo, disclosed that from the physical inspection conducted on the body, police found two cuts one on the neck and another on the stomach.

Mr Namalongo said the incident is reported to have occurred between 04:00 hours and 07:00 hours on September 9, 2026.

The Commissioner said that on September 9, 2026, at 08:00 hours, the victim’s mother, Mildred Yomena, 49, reported that her daughter had been found dead inside her house.

“Brief facts are that Ms Yomena, who reported the matter to police, was at home when she received a telephone call from a concerned member of the public informing her that her daughter had been found dead inside her house.

She immediately rushed to the house, where she found her daughter lying in a pool of blood. A knife with blood stains was found near the deceased’s head. She then rushed to Shampande Police Post and reported the matter,” Mr Namalongo said.

Mr Namalongo disclosed that the deceased’s 50‑year‑old husband has since been apprehended and is detained in police custody in connection with the murder of Ms Mudenda.

Investigations into the matter are ongoing.

Mr Namalongo said the body was later taken to Choma General Hospital, where death was certified, and was subsequently deposited in the mortuary awaiting a postmortem examination.

The Commissioner further disclosed that the suspect remains in custody as investigations into the matter continue.

World.title: Mozambique congratulates Zambia for peaceful election
World.content:
The Mozambican government has congratulated the people of Zambia for conducting peaceful elections that resulted in the re-election of President Hakainde Hichilema.

Mozambique’s Permanent Secretary in the Ministry of Interior, Victor Domingos Canhemba Jr, says that the re-election of President Hichilema presents an opportunity to enhance the defense and security relations currently prevailing between Zambia and Mozambique.

Speaking during the official opening of the Senior Officials Meeting of the 14th Mozambique-Zambia Joint Permanent Commission on Defence and Security in Maputo, Mozambique, this morning, Mr Canhemba Jr, expressed hope that the re-election of President Hichilema will help the two nations continue working together to maintain regional stability.

Mr Canhemba Jr, who is chairing the Senior Officials Meeting, commended Zambians for conducting peaceful elections.

Meanwhile, Zambia Air Force (ZAF) Commander Lieutenant General Oscar Nyoni has called for enhanced efforts to combat transnational crime between the two countries.

Lt. Gen. Nyoni, who serves as Co-Chairman of the Senior Officials Meeting, cautioned that unaddressed security challenges could jeopardize peace.

The ZAF Commander called for strengthened coordination between Zambia and Mozambique.

The Zambia Air Force Commander is leading the Zambian delegation to the meeting.

Prominent members of the delegation include Zambia’s Ambassador to Mozambique, Derrick Livune; Ministry of Defence Director of Research, Planning, and Projects, Ireen Habasimbi; Zambia Correctional Service Deputy Commissioner General, Bwalya Kuyomba; and Ministry of Home Affairs and Internal Security Director of Research and Planning, Goodson Sinyenga.

This is contained in a statement issued to the Zambia News and Information Services (ZANIS) in Lusaka today, by Ministry of Defense Principle Public Relations Officer, Paul Shalala.

World.title: 2-year-old girl defiled
World.content:
Police in Sinda District have nabbed a 19- year-old male of Chimbete Village in Chieftainess Nyanje for allegedly defiling a 2-year-old girl child.

Eastern Province Police Commanding Officer Robertson Mweemba has named the suspect as Richard Banda who was apprehended with the help of the community on Tuesday, September 8, 2026 at around 18:00 hours when he attempted to flee.

Mr Mweemba revealed that the suspect was caught with the assistance of community members who were alerted by the victims grandfather after he noticed him on top of the child on the veranda of his house.

“The suspect was entrusted with the child by her father to escort her to the mother between 13:00 and 14:00 hours before he diverted and had carnal knowledge of a child,” he said.

It is reported that the suspect had been drinking the whole morning of the incident.

The victim sustained bruised private parts and remains admitted to Nyanje Mission Hospital.

“A docket case has been opened, as the suspect remains in custody as he is expected to appear in court,” Mr Mweemba said.

World.title: Zambia signs 540,000 metric tonnes maize export deal with Kenya
World.content:
Government has signed an agreement with Kenya’s Baita Trading Limited for the export of up to 540,000 metric tonnes of Grade A, white non-GMO maize, in a development expected to boost agricultural exports, create a market for farmers and strengthen regional food security.

The agreement between the Food Reserve Agency (FRA) and Baita Trading Limited of Kenya comes as Zambia records a bumper maize harvest of more than 5.1 million metric tonnes in the 2025/2026 farming season.

This bumper harvest provided the country with adequate stocks for domestic consumption and a surplus for export.

Speaking during the signing ceremony in Lusaka today, Deputy Secretary to the Cabinet for Finance and Economic Development, Siazongo Siakalenge, said the maize surplus presents an opportunity for Zambia to earn foreign exchange while supporting farmers and contributing to economic growth.

Mr Siakalenge said the government has been working to secure export markets for the surplus maize and has so far identified several opportunities, with the latest agreement providing a significant market for Zambian grain.

“The country has enough food to feed itself, as well as a surplus to export and to earn revenue for the country. This surplus generates foreign exchange for the country and thereby contributes to economic and financial stability,” he said.

Mr Siakalenge noted that the availability of adequate maize stocks is also expected to contribute to stable maize prices while creating opportunities for traders and other private-sector players to participate in the export market.

He noted that Zambia’s agricultural exports increased from US$967 million in 2024 to more than US$1.1 billion in 2025, with the maize export agreement expected to contribute to further growth in the sector.

And FRA Board Chairperson, Suresh Desai, said the agreement demonstrates continued confidence in the quality of Zambian agricultural produce and is in line with the government’s ambition of increasing maize production to 10 million metric tonnes per annum.

Mr Desai said increased production must be matched with reliable markets and efficient logistics to ensure that farmers benefit from expanded production.

“What we are witnessing here today is part and parcel of that stated policy of taking the production of maize in Zambia to 10 million metric tonnes per annum,” he said.

Mr Desai said the 540,000 metric tonnes will be moved in five tranches to allow the parties to effectively manage transportation and logistics, while the pricing of each tranche will be determined through an agreed mechanism based on prevailing regional market prices.

He has further commended the government, FRA management and the technical teams from Zambia and Kenya for successfully negotiating the agreement, saying the initiative will promote mutually beneficial trade and support the livelihoods of Zambian farmers.

Meanwhile, Baita Trading Limited Director, Martin Kinoti, said the company is pleased to be part of the agreement and has commended the Zambian government and FRA for facilitating the process.

Mr Kinoti noted that the focus will now shift from negotiations to implementation, with the private sector expected to play a key role in ensuring that the maize reaches the Kenyan market.

He explained that the agreement is not only about supplying grain to Kenya but also about strengthening relations between the two countries and promoting regional food security, particularly as Kenya faces recurring drought challenges.

“We are looking forward to shifting to the performance of this agreement, which is the next thing that we will be spending our energies on,” Mr Kinoti said.

World.title: Illegal miner dies
World.content:
A 24‑year‑old miner of Vubwi District in Eastern Province has died after he was trapped in a tunnel that collapsed on him.

The accident, which occurred at Kamudothi Mine, involved seven other miners who escaped unhurt.

Eastern Province Police Commanding Officer Robertson Mweemba confirmed the incident, saying it happened around 18:00 hours on Tuesday in Chithumba area.

Mr Mweemba identified the deceased as Daniel Nyirenda of Magazine Compound in Chipata District.

He said Nyirenda was in a seven‑metre‑deep tunnel with seven other illegal miners when a loose upper layer of stones collapsed at the deepest end of the tunnel.

“Whilst they were busy digging underground and loading the mineral ores in sacks to be lifted above ground, a loose upper layer of stone piles started collapsing at the deep end of the tunnel,” Mr Mweemba said.

He said the seven other miners managed to escape, but Nyirenda could not get out before the collapse.

“The seven others managed to get out of the tunnel in time, while male Daniel Nyirenda could not get out on time and the pile of soil collapsed on him,” he said.

Mr Mweemba said the other miners later dug Nyirenda out of the collapsed tunnel and rushed him to Mlawe Rural Health Post where he was pronounced dead upon arrival.

Police officers who visited the scene found Nyirenda’s body at Mlawe Rural Health Post.

A physical inspection revealed multiple cuts on the head, a broken right leg and a deep cut on the left leg.

Mr Mweemba said police do not suspect foul play in the death.

“The body was deposited into Chipata general hospital mortuary awaiting burial arrangements,” he said.

World.title: Maggie Sapatu returns home
World.content:
Maggie Sapatu, a 52‑year‑old woman of Mwinilunga District in Northwestern Province who braved the odds by walking from Mwinilunga to Lusaka to meet President Hakainde Hichilema after his victory in the August 13 general elections that secured him a second term in office, has returned home.

Ms Sapatu was received today at Solwezi Airport by North‑Western Province Permanent Secretary Colonel Grandson Katambi (retired), who was flanked by his Deputy Luckson Mulumbi, Kalumbila District Commissioner Brenda Sankisa and other officials.

Speaking on arrival, Ms Sapatu said she embarked on the journey to meet the Head of State to appreciate him for the massive development he has achieved and for promoting peace and unity in the country.

She further called on people across the country to rally behind President Hakainde Hichilema and work with him to make Zambia a better country for all.

And Col Katambi has hailed Ms Sapatu for taking a bold step to walk to Lusaka stating that her bravery is commendable and represents the appreciation of the exceptional leadership of President Hakainde Hichilema.

The Permanent Secretary said the gesture by Ms Sapato demonstrates that women in Northwestern Province appreciate the efforts government is making to develop not only the region but the country as a whole.
